Those three are really capable people. If they believe the Guards, then there's no reason for us not to.
I g—guess...
Fidora's right. They saved lots of people at the mines... I think they can be trusted.
The dumpster remains silent. This hunk of junk gazes gently at you.

You feel a sense of relief when you stand before this dumpster. "It's all over," breathes Belobog's winter, "This is the last one." Your feeling no longer matters. What matters is that the ones who created these trashcans have fulfilled themselves.
The dumpster stands silently, yet a hint of sinister comes through.
A scientist once said, "When a dumpster is shut tight, it exists in a superposition of states where it is both devoid of trash and full of trash at the same time."
You vaguely recall a television series where a lawyer hid inside a dumpster such as this and waited for an incriminating piece of evidence to appear out of thin air.
You vaguely recall a television series where a homeless kid hid inside a dumpster like this, tightly covered his mouth, and waited for his armed pursuers to leave.
You vaguely recall a video game in which the protagonist hid inside one of these dumpsters and quietly took out the enemy when they approached.

You vaguely recall a video game in which a destitute police officer could not afford to pay for the night's room and dove into a dumpster like this amidst the taunting laughter of the shopkeeper — and apparently got an achievement out of it.
You vaguely recall a video game in which a key item can be found in dumpsters like this to solve a puzzle and unlock the next area.
You don't understand where your obsession with dumpsters come from, but it must have to do with the aforementioned work.

A huge dumpster filled to the brim. The mixture of all kinds of trash results in a putrid odor. However, those who live in the Underworld have some consolation: They don't need to go through the trouble of sorting their garbage.
A huge dumpster. If you caught a cold, you can even use it as a capsule hotel.
The opened lid of the dumpster seems to be urging you to leave the unconscious bodies of the patrolling soldiers inside.
There are two types of heroes in this world: One of them hides in the dumpster before they were seen, and the other hides bodies in the dumpster before they were seen.
This trashcan is huge, but its inside is empty. Life is no different.
You see a pitiful trashcan made of tin, with a torso clearly dented from trauma. It seems like someone took their pent-up emotions on it whilst passing by.
The two trashcans stood tightly side by side as if no force in the world could separate them.
The two trashcans stood tightly side by side, their shadows meld together as if they were locked in an embrace.
The two trashcans stood tightly side by side. If one of them falls, the other will surely follow.
The two trashcans stood tightly side by side. This might be one of the most beautiful things in the world, to have another self standing by your side, even if it is just a trashcan.
As long as trashcans stand together, they can weather all difficulties in the universe.

The trashcan glared coldly at the other trashcan gasping for air at its feet. "I told you, Tatalov," it said. "I told you that you will one day collapse beside me. When that time comes, I will laugh to your dying face. Such is the wind of change."

A goo of darkness dripped out of the dying trashcan's form and continued to snake its way forward. It looked up at the cold eyes of the other trashcan. Fifteen years had passed since it had last seen that gaze, when the standing trashcan was still tiny.

"It's me..." the dying trashcan bade, "I was the one... who raised you..." A wave of sharp pain enveloped it. At that moment, it realized that a certain trash bag had burst. The shooting pain coaxed a whimper out of the dying trashcan while the other one snickered satisfactorily.

It crouched down and whispered a name in the ear of the dying trashcan. "You—" The trashcan's eyes were wide open. "But— No, you can't be..." Its final words curdled inside its mouth, just like the teardrop hanging from the corner of its eye.
The road closure barrier always leaves you with an infinite reverie about the future.
Maybe some day in the future, the metal barriers will disappear from this world, opening doors toward a future possibility.
This is a street lamp, this description should suffice.
Why are you investigating a street lamp? It doesn't do anything.
Spend some time on the things that might have a reward, this is only a street lamp.
This street lamp will not drop items or material, and it will not unlock a new mission.
A street lamp, it plays the part of a zeitgeber in the dim underground.
A street lamp, costs <unbreak>700</unbreak> shield.
This mailbox is tucked away in the corner, trying not to be noticed. "Better not disturb it." You get the sense that even the most sociable person would need some personal space, let alone a mailbox.

Composing a piece of mail requires time, and so does mailing it. Written mail's value comes with its temporal investment. Who would derive excitement from that which is of low-value? It's just a tap and a swipe, like the text message from your friend you didn't bother to reply.
Just a normal mailbox.
Mining tools are scattered around the clinic's entrance.
You see a pickaxe. Its pointed end resembles the beak of a crane, so it is also colloquially called a cranebeak. A common tool used for gardening and mining.
Mining tools are laid haphazardly on the roadside.
There are discolored patches on the wooden handles of these tools, telling the tale of their owner's hard work.
You try to pick up a shovel with one hand and are immediately thrown off-balance by its weight.
Some of these tools had their owner's name carved on them. They were probably very well taken care of.
You see a weathered shovel, the head of which has been gnawed and scarred by the sharp rocks.
You see a pickaxe in near-pristine condition, both of its points barely having any scratches on them.
Crystalline ores sparkle inside the crate.
The wooden crate carries a kind of ore called Geomarrow, an excellent energy source.

Geomarrow, as the name suggests, is the essence of the planet. To Jarilo-VI and Belobog, it is an invaluable treasure. However, ores will run out one day, and what will happen then? No one knows, and no one wants to know.
The Geomarrow ore was cut into a cuboid, or maybe it was formed into this elegant shape naturally.
Geomarrow, one of the few still-usable energy sources on this planet. After the blockade was implemented, only this type of ore was allowed to return to the Overworld.
Smart miners will use these mine carts to make their work easier, but it remains up for debate whether it makes their work smarter.
You have a feeling that this thing will cause you problems in the future.
The poster seems to be tantalizing you to join the Fight Club.

When people talk about fighting, they are referring to one of three things: Punching techniques, palm strikes, and finger strikes. If fighting sports are too heavy for you, you can start with rock, paper, scissors.
Fighting, also known as brawling. It is not just a scuffle, but a healthy, physical and mental athletic sport that promotes sportsmanship.
The blower whirrs and drums. Maybe they were trying to cheer for you.
You see a sandbag, its job is to take a beating.
You see a sandbag that works <unbreak>24</unbreak>/7. It never complains, is full of damage, was never compensated, and still had to be looked down on. You hope that it can stand up on its own.
What you learned from observing the sandbag: It pays to be heavy. When people are attacking you, their hands will hurt.
What you learned from observing the sandbag: If you don't make a sound, no one would know how much pain you're in.
What you learned from observing the sandbag: Your pain will likely be another person's experience.
What you learned from observing the sandbag: When assaulted with blows, try to move with the force and counterattack using momentum.
What you learned from observing the sandbag: Commit to your choices, even if you're falling. Stylistic theatrics is just a waste of time that no one appreciates.
All sorts of posters, invitations, and notices are plastered upon this wall. One caught your attention. It looks new, but there are an abundance of dirty fingerprints on it.
It is clear that for many people, this Boxer Recruitment Form had ignited their fighting spirit.
All forms of papers have been chaotically taped on this patchy wall. With just one look at it, you can almost hear the cacophony that saturated the space.

You will never be able to see a wall like this in Belobog: Sheets of paper occupy every inch of its surface like moss. The walls of the Overworld are classical and stately, while those in the Underworld exude a unique, quaint poignancy.

You see an extremely aggressive poster. Everything about it, from its color choice, to its provocative text, to the fist illustration as large as a sandbag, they all ooze strongly of combative passion.
This old dumpster stands silently, carrying its own resolute gravitas that reminds you of an elder of vast wisdom. It stood on the side of the street for years, witnessing its rise and fall.
Great, I will open it.
Uh, you may have missed the narration just now: This elderly dumpster had been standing in this spot for years. You must respect its years of accumulated wisdom.
I have no idea what you're saying...
Do. Not. Open. This dumpster up. Just let it stand in its place quietly, respectably, alright?
Are you trying to stop me?

You are unstoppable, alright? Your will is absolute. This is just a piece of advice: Please refrain from uncovering the dumpster's contents and just let it stand here with the silence and dignity it deserves.
I still want to open it, I've made up my mind.

Of course, you can do whatever you want: Look! The dumpster lid opens under your absolute will. There is nothing inside, absolutely nothing, but look on the bright side! You have imposed your might unto it. This is the most important aspect in any game!
Sure, I will take back my insistence.

That is wise. You are an open-minded person who readily accepts opinions of others, and Elder Dumpster silently tip its figurative hat at you. You feel the hefty history of its existence emanate outward in every direction, echoing in the depths of the earth.
Fine, I won't touch it.

You leave it alone. You walk away resolutely, but even with the distance you have put between you, you still feel the heft of its history emanating outward from the dumpster, echoing in the depths of the earth.
I pay respects to it.
You bow at Elder Dumpster, to which it responds with a deep dignity, it almost feels like it is the size of two dumpsters.

This dumpster evokes a special emotion in you. Unrelated to its location, appearance, and olfactory triggers, it is a sense of hiding from the world as well as a hint of preternatural coziness. A wrinkly piece of paper is stuck on the lid of the dumpster with the number "<unbreak>81</unbreak>" on it.
Open.

You see a shabby room with a set of wrinkled yellowish bedding, a pillow made from a gunny sack, two opened bread-flavor soda, a pair of miner's boots, a torn out book whose words can no longer be distinguished, as well as a knife.
Looks like someone used this dumpster as their humble living quarters.
Knock on it.

Well behaved! This trashcan is someone's private zone. *rat-a-tat-tat* Knocking on the wall before entering represents your respect. In fact, however, not every decent person can really win others' respect.
Open.

You see a shabby room with a set of wrinkled yellowish bedding, a pillow made from a gunny sack, two opened bread-flavor soda, a pair of miner's boots, a torn out book whose words can no longer be distinguished, as well as a knife.
Looks like someone used this dumpster as their humble living quarters.
Scribble the paper.

You changed the number on this piece of paper to <unbreak>84</unbreak>. You may have done this out of no reason, but you have a feeling that this has changed many things. A package will be forever lost in the underground. An iron bottle will fall. Someone will cry.
This is merely your feeling, which does not represent reality, but you do feel a little uneasy because of your tiny prank. Regrettably, you cannot witness the consequences.
Leave.
You leave this dumpster and forget all about it.
Scribble the paper.

You changed the number on this piece of paper to <unbreak>84</unbreak>. You may have done this out of no reason, but you have a feeling that this has changed many things. A package will be forever lost in the underground. An iron bottle will fall. Someone will cry.
This is merely your feeling, which does not represent reality, but you do feel a little uneasy because of your tiny prank. Regrettably, you cannot witness the consequences.
Leave.
You leave this dumpster and forget all about it.

The dumpster is shining. Someone threw three pieces of Geomarrow in it. The person threw it so heavily that shards of the ore scattered all over the trashcan. You have no idea where the anger of that person stems from, neither can you understand this behavior. After all, Geomarrow is as valuable as gold in the underground. Would you throw money even in a fit of anger?
Of course.
Wow.
Certainly not.
That's right! Now, let's end the conversation here. It's really boring to talk about dumpsters and money.

This trashcan looks just like the other ones at first glance, but when you take a closer look, you uncover its sinister nature: Someone has done something to the spring bar of the lid. If you push the lid of this trashcan, the lid will be bounce back to you, dealing a heavy blow.
Fix it.
You spent some time on it but finally succeeded. Now the spring bar is fixed and nobody will be hurt by this trashcan.
Temper it.
Are you serious? Oh my, this is a truly evil trick. High Morals would despise such behavior. You have to consume a Praise of High Morals to recompense for it. Are you willing to?
Do it!

The High Morals are sad, but admittedly, your trick is quite brilliant. Now, when the lid bounces back, The two packs of oil will be split all over the unlucky person's clothes. Aha would applaud such a prank.
Do it!

You want to conduct something so mischievous, but you are unable to do it. Or you can put it that way: You have never received the Praise of High Morals. In that case, if you insist on doing bad things, it will be really upset.
I quit!
You leave this dumpster and forget all about it.
None of my business.
You leave this dumpster and forget all about it.

The big trashcan lies in plain air. You can see that it has been filled with citizens' discarded trash. Suddenly, you hear a voice saying: "Trailblazer, do you want these seven normal pieces of trash or this beautiful piece of trash?"
Seven normal pieces of trash.
"You are an honest person," the voice says in an approving way, "I will give you what you want."
One beautiful piece of trash.
"You are an honest person," the voice says in an approving way, "I will give you what you want."
I want them all.
"You are a greedy person," the voice says in an approving way, "I will give you what you want."
I don't want any trash!
"You are a simple person," the voice says in an approving way, "I will give you what you want."
Game time. Guess: How many trashcans are there in Belobog? Attention: Trashcans put side-by-side together are considered as one. But, those that you can see but cannot be reached do not count.
<unbreak>19</unbreak>.
<unbreak>20</unbreak>.
<unbreak>21</unbreak>.

Nice answer! Honestly, it is uncertain if your answer is correct. This is the Underworld, after all. This trashcan has not seen its Overworld relatives in a long time. You know what, here comes a question with a definite answer!

Guess: How many trashcans are there in this town? The rules are the same: Trashcans placed side-by-side are considered as one. But, those that you can see but cannot be reached do not count. Count only these: Cylindrical trashcans.

Wow! You really do take note of each interactable trashcan... You are correct! Five is the correct answer! This trashcan brims with happiness because of your attention, even the garbage inside it is becoming more beautiful.
This is the wrong answer, but it is understandable. Who would count the number of existing trashcans? So, let's stop this game right now. It's too childish! Childish!
This is the wrong answer, but it is understandable. Who would count the number of existing trashcans? So, let's stop this game right now. It's too childish! Childish!
How would I know? This is not fair!
The trashcan thinks you're right, this isn't fair. Who would count the number of existing trashcans? So, let's stop this game right now. It's too childish! Childish!
This is a trashcan, its lid seems to have been cut open with some kind of implement.
Open it.

You open the tin lid and a waft of burnt wood mixed with cold steel invades your olfactory senses. Looking into the depth of the trashcan, you can see flickers of embers still hanging on, struggling to extend their own lifespan.
This is normal.
It is just a lobotomized trashcan, there are many of them across the universe. "What do I have against trashcans?" You find yourself thinking before leaving with your comrades.
Passing by this pitiful mailbox, you catch a glimmer of what does not belong — the corner of a yellowing envelope hanging limply on the edge of its opening.
Take it out.

You rescue the fragile envelope — this is not a hyperbole, the envelope is disintegrating. The paper scraps crumble into thin air, merging with the unique mine dust, then disappear into the abyss of scorching air. Before its final act of glory, your actions gave it salvation.
Push it in.

You lightly press against the envelope and push it into the dark and unknowable depths of the mailbox. Like a pebble dropped into the ocean, it lost connection with the outside world the moment it vanished into the abyss.
I have bigger fish to fry.

You hear a deep voice resonating deep within your heart. "Why waste the effort?" Another voice follows, "That's right!" You don't know where the voices come from, but they undoubtedly arrived at the same conclusion and made the decision for you.
<unbreak>23</unbreak>:<unbreak>47</unbreak>:<unbreak>15</unbreak> system time. Very punctual, Kafka.
{RUBY_B#Stellaron Hunter}Elio{RUBY_E#} always tells the exact future. So what's with the explosion just now? Was that also part of his script?
Uh-huh — "<unbreak>23</unbreak>:<unbreak>44</unbreak>:<unbreak>59</unbreak> system time: The pulses from the explosion cause a massive breakdown from the master control system."
You did that?
No, the Antimatter Legion did it. They completely invaded the space station two system hours ago.
*whistle* Alright, so do we need to fight the Legion?
I dunno. Elio didn't say anything about it, so it doesn't matter.
Got it. So from now on, I'll be in charge of this operation.
Copy. Can you let me have some fun this time? Our last few operations turned out to be pretty dull.
...Sorry, I'm afraid there's not much I can do for you — our task this time is just to "place" the target properly.
But if you wanna go look for some fun yourself, I won't stop you. I mean, after all...
So the owner of this space station is Herta, No. <unbreak>83</unbreak> of the Genius Society, right? Is her security system easy to crack?
Not really. But the Legion's invasion paralyzed the master control system for a few minutes, which was a big help.
I guess this space station is about to meet its doom now that it's become a target of the Aeon of {RUBY_B#Nanook}Destruction{RUBY_E#}.
...No, it isn't. There's a sequel to this mission... You didn't read the script?
...You know me, I hate being told what to do. Elio knows this too, so he normally just tells me what's off-limits.
Like what?
Like wiping this place out.
*sigh* Yeah, yeah. Where did you send it, Silver Wolf?
Some random coordinates, not important. You care about where that Voidranger ended up?
Of course not~ I'm just amazed at this fancy technique of yours, as usual.
Just a little trick of tampering with the data of reality, I wouldn't call it fancy.
What were you looking at so intently just now? Let me see.
Herta's toys, a catalog featuring the space station's collection of rare items. They've got a lot of interesting gadgets.
Like what?
There's this gun, it can rate any creature within its crosshair as a score from 0 to <unbreak>100</unbreak>.
...Doesn't sound very interesting.
Aren't you curious about how much you would score? I kinda wanna know mine.
Fine, I guess we can swing by and play with it if it's not too far. What's our destination?
Go down the corridor behind the door on the left. There's a room where some kind of rare item is stored.
So that's where the {RUBY_B#Cancer of All Worlds}Stellaron{RUBY_E#} is?
That's where we can find out where the Stellaron is.
Is the receptacle ready for use?
Of course. You just need to make the decision.
Elio said this decision will bring about lots of changes...
He also said it must be you who makes it.
When did the Antimatter Legion become so weak?
I could only attract this much. Did you really want the entire Legion to come here?
This lot won't be able to slow down the Astral Express crew.
Relax. A Doomsday Beast is also here.
Wanna give {M#him}{F#her} a new name?
Hmm...
Alright, that's it.
You can still change your mind before we find the Stellaron.
We're getting close to the central area of the space station, the main force of the Legion must be there.
Not a problem, for us.
Just a reminder — this is a stealth mission, Kafka.
No one will know we were here if they are all dead.
The central area of the space station is up ahead. There will be lots of Legion Voidrangers there.
Okay~
Hold it.
Someone, or something, is up ahead.
Looks like we're the ones getting ambushed.
But they're the ones getting besieged.
Not a single soul here. Impressive evacuation work. Did Herta organize it herself?
According to the access history, she hasn't logged in here for over six months. The evacuation was directed by the acting lead researcher — a girl named Asta.
Doesn't ring a bell. Oh, right, Elio said we wouldn't run into Herta. It seems she really isn't here.
Where's the {RUBY_B#Cancer of All Worlds}Stellaron{RUBY_E#}?
Elio's script doesn't include any info about the location of the Stellaron, which means in the future he foresees...
...We would find the Stellaron in a non-physical way?
This space station is packed with extraordinary objects, I wouldn't be surprised if there's one that can make it happen.
Hiding something extraordinary with something extraordinary... this is pretty Herta. I assume you know what to do? I mean, you've read that catalog for quite a while.
I've got all the clues we need. The only piece missing is a simple trick.
Help me investigate the terminal in this room, our item might be inside.
Okay, the stage is yours~
I can see the whole space station on the surveillance screen... but not the Stellaron.
Even if you could, it'd be a trap. Herta doesn't display her collections.
Huh? I can't see the memory storage for this terminal...
This is the monitoring room, they must have deleted the records and made a run for it. Classic.
*sigh* Make your way over here then, there's no point in trying to search like this.
Well? Found anything?
Do you know how many monitors are in the room?
I don't know, and don't need to know.
What's so important about investigating this?
So you won't get bored.
Is Herta's security system really that difficult to crack?
It's definitely not easy... but whatever.
The Legion's invasion paralyzed the master control system for a few minutes, which was a big help.
Done. Come over.
Everything's ready. You can stop your investigation.
(It just looks like an ordinary terminal. There's nothing unusual on the screen...)
So, got a master plan? I'm all ears.
It's a matter of hacking the surveillance system directly.
Aha, I see. Herta's collections aren't in the system, so anything unaffected should be our target.
Simple, crude, but effective. Look, found it.
Huh. What's this?

Item number <unbreak>211</unbreak>, "Blind Spot": A simple light-deflecting field. It allows an object in its field to pass unnoticed, but if a different item ceases to be obvious, the object gets revealed.
So Herta hides her collection with something as simple as this?
The simplest method is the hardest to spot, isn't that our motto?
*whistle* Strange thing number two...
The data suggests it's just an ordinary hologram. But it has an added layer...
Let's take a look. Don't worry, this place won't be our grave.
Hey, did you notice that one of the monsters you just defeated had a different body build? Even the joint on its left leg looked different from the others.
I'm pretty sure that's what... what killed Alfred!
I did it! I finally did it! I finally avenged Alfred!
I had to gather up so much courage to come do Mr. Wen's errands, and who knew it would turn out to be an avenging trip? Is this fate? *sniff*
Running errands for Mr. Wen?
Yep, Mr. Wen asked me to go to the Curio Sorting Room in the Storage Zone to pick up an item for him.
Mr. Wen said you were missing.
Mr. Wen said I was missing? But he was the one who sent me here to fetch stuff for him.
You almost died!
Life is but a path to death... Besides, I'm still pretty alive now.
The way you care so much about me reminds me of Alfred... Now, my wish is finally fulfilled.
But before I return, I still have to pick up a thing for Mr. Wen in the Curio Sorting Room.
He said you were missing.
Mr. Wen said I was missing? But he was the one who sent me here.
This makes no sense... Look, he also gave me this executive order.
See? This is the executive order that Mr. Wen personally gave me. It's a notice of an Ad Hoc Transfer. All written in black and white, clear as day.
So even boxers can be Curio?
Are they not!? If it's just an ordinary pair of boxers, why would Mr. Wen ask me to pick them up?
Your name is Aburgerham?
Maybe Mr. Wen was so busy with his chores and stuff that he made an honest mistake.
You actually believe that!?
The order was handed to me by Mr. Wen Mingde himself. It can't be a mistake.
I still remember that his pupils were dilated, head covered in sweat, hands cold, and even his throat made a faint gurgling sound.
He must've been really eager to get the Curio, so I have to get this done for him...
This smells fishy!
Why are you so weird about this? You aren't freaked out by the monsters like I was before, are you?
Let's go back and check this with Mr. Wen.
I don't think this is a good idea. Mr. Wen Mingde personally gave me the task, and I can't just go back without completing it first...
Then go and fetch your thing.
Why the change? Weird... You aren't freaked out by the monsters like I was before?
Anyway, it's safe here. I'll go and get the Curio soon.
If you have any doubts, just take this transfer order. Go back and ask Mr. Wen Mingde about it...
Drop the act, already.
You drop the act.
I know it's you. You've been pretending to be me, deceiving everyone with your shenanigans. And now you have the audacity to stand here in front of me.

Excuse me, but who are you calling a fake? I was standing right here the whole time. You're the one who just appeared out of nowhere. I have witnesses who can confirm that. So tell me, who do you think looks suspicious here? You or me?

Now, everyone, the situation is clear as day. It's already well-known that <color=#dbc291ff>Xenohydro</color> has been on the loose for a long time. Xenohydro can change its form and mimic others' appearances so perfectly that it's virtually impossible to tell the difference...
But I never would have thought that this creature would be so bold, approaching us like this and trying to take my place.
Don't try to steal my words. You accused me of being fake, but do you have any proof to back up your claim?
What about your claim? And where is the evidence to support it?
{NICKNAME}, you arrive just in time. What do you think?
Ugh. I should probably leave.
Wait, don't just leave. You're now the only one who can prove that I am really me. I am the real Wen Mingde, who just spoke with you earlier. Remember?
By the way, where's Abraham? Did you find him?
I might have a way to solve this.
What is it then? Spit it out. I don't want to waste any more time with that thing!
By the way, where's Abraham? Did you find him?
You guys should fight it out.
Ugh, you really don't care, do you?
By the way, where's Abraham? Did you find him?
And what's this transfer order in your hands...
Retrieve the <color=#dbc291ff>Boxer with Colored Tortoiseshell Pattern</color>... You cheeky Xenohydro! How dare you use my identity to steal such a valuable Curio!
Now that the evidence is all clear, it's time to end this. I suggest {NICKNAME} make the call.
I agree. {NICKNAME}, what do you say?
We should check the vital signs.
We've done that already. The team here has checked our pupils, sweat glands, voice, and body temperature.
But perhaps the tension was simply too high to act normally. Our pupils were both dilated, we were both sweating profusely, our voices were trembling, and our bodies were cold to the touch.
Ugh! Wish I wasn't so worked up, otherwise we would've been able to tell by now.
Check the signature.
Don't waste your time. The note signed "Wen Mingy" was obviously a blatant mockery of me by the Xenohydro.
He can imitate my looks and personality really well, so I don't think that handwriting will be too difficult for him either.
I noticed both of us are carrying the written orders for the team's daily attendance, which you can review at will.
We should check the boxers!
Those boxers are a Curio and are not to be worn! Not to mention that they are not my personal property. What's there to check!

These boxers are clearly planted by the Xenohydro! I, Wen Mingde, the dignified leader of the Department of Implement Arts and head of the Curio Collection Squad, will not allow the Xenohydro to mock me like this!
That's it for now.
{NICKNAME}, what do you think?
(Wait and see)
*sigh* Can't believe I'm gonna say this, but the easiest way is to arrest both of us.
What do you mean?
At this point, I must stop the Xenohydro from further harming the space station. To protect the whole team, I am willing to sacrifice my own freedom.
Don't act so holier-than-thou...
I also think that, if we're locked up long enough, the Xenohydro will get bored eventually and show its true colors.
I see. So you are just trying to drag me into the same miserable situation as you.
Even if I get locked up in the containment chamber, I can still lead the Curio retrieval efforts.
Ugh. I don't wanna go back!
What did you just say?
<color=#dbc291ff>"Go back"</color>? Everybody heard him. He admitted it!
All's fair in love and war.
Seriously!?
Hehe, hehehe, Mr. Wen Mingy, your willingness to "sacrifice" yourself like that is quite touching, isn't it?
I only wanted to tease you a bit. Never expected to catch so much attention.
Unfortunately for you, I won't give up that easily—
(Try to dupe him)
After so many questions, I think you would've made your choice, no?
I don't think {F#she}{M#he} has.
Don't listen to him. It's up to {NICKNAME} to make the call. Who's real and who's fake?
The one on the left?
Haha! I knew I was right about you. Good choice, good choice!
Ugh, why should we trust your judgment? You are a stinky outsider who came out of nowhere...
Don't be a sore loser.
Huh? His pupils are dilating abnormally. Sweat is quickly secreting all over his body, and his hair is wet...
He is the Xenohydro!
Ha! So it worked!
Actually, that was a random pick.
*gurgle*... You spoiled my plan. This is not fun...
How dare you expose me? I'll make you pay...
The one on the right?
Hee, hee hee, you made the right choice. Hurry up and lock up the fake on the opposite side, *gurgle*...
I'm not the Xenohydro! Wait a minute, did anyone hear him make that weird noise?
Don't waste your time, *gurgle*. Even {NICKNAME} says you're a fake, *gurgle*...
That's the watery, guttural sound unique to the Xenohydro!
*gurgle*... I got carried away. Never could've thought I'd fail at the last minute...
Well, I guess I got it right after all.
Ugh, at least keep the act till the end.
Well, I guess I'll have to sort you out.
Fall in and count!
The numbers are right, not one more, not one less. Alas, the Xenohydro had escaped.
Hurry up and chase it!
There's no point. The Xenohydro must have disguised itself as a staff member already. Probably already out of the storage zone and on the way to other places.
We're so close.
It's all my fault. Now, how should I explain this to Lead Researcher Asta...
Hey, we learn from our mistakes. It is imperative to set up a secret code within the squad to prevent the same farce from ever happening again.
I will report this to Mrs. Hinkel and ask her to assign more staff to apprehend the Xenohydro as soon as possible.
Sorry to get you involved in this fuss. Here's a little something for your trouble. It's not much, but please accept it.
If you ever find the Xenohydro elsewhere, remember that the Curio Collection Squad is always here. Don't try to fight it alone. Everyone, fall in!
The Xenohydro's combat abilities have been neutralized.
Everyone, fall in an olive-shaped formation! And use the central elevator as our starting point! Prepare for the collection process! Pay attention to anyone suspicious around you!
(There is a burst of chaotic activity and everything was a blur. Something seems to be moving fast!)
(... The chaos gradually subsides.)
You move pretty quick, {F#lass}{M#lad}. There are lots of nice things in these boxes here. Help yourself.
I am in a hurry. Bye!
Why didn't you just turn on the switch yourself?
Why didn't I turn it on myself... Hoho, I suppose I didn't notice.
What about the big reward you promised me?
What a big reward... I don't remember making such a promise.
Such terrible acting...
What? I can't hear you clearly, {F#lass}{M#lad}. Speak up!
... Forget it, as long as you're fine.
Of course I'm fine! Every muscle and bone, everything is fine.
So you just wanted to get my attention.
No. I did not. Don't be ridiculous, {F#lass}{M#lad}.
You're not trying to blackmail me... are you?
I didn't ask for anything! How can you call this blackmail? At most I just took up a little of your time.
Come on, get out of the way, I can't hold it anymore. Come get me in the maintenance room if you need anything!
Look, I don't know for how long this bottle-opener has been in the toolbox. I finally found it!
This bottle of soda is from four Amber Eras ago, <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color>, so fragrant. Ho... so refreshing!
Would you like a sip?
Just one sip!
Good one, kid! You have no idea how frustrated I was just now. I had this tasty treat in my hand, but I couldn't drink it! I almost tried to pry it open with my teeth!
It's my own fault for bringing it with me when I went down to unblock those bearings. Why did I forget the bottle opener?
Must've gone flat ages ago, right?
I haven't gone flat! When I was your age, I could light Gunn's beard on fire and set up Bernard with that chick in the Department of Insight, all in one go!
Sadly, I really was a bit flat in the "Station Breakout" incident.
Time flies, though. Now, I even forget to bring a bottle opener. I can't deny I am old.
So this is why you were in a hurry...
Ha, what did you expect? Can't I reward myself with a bottle of soda after working so hard dealing with that blockage?
I just forgot to bring the opener. Sigh... I must admit I am old.

Let me tell you, the patent for this <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color> used to belong to the space station. This anti-gravity drink was once all the rage across the cosmos. I only have a few bottles left.
I'd better enjoy every last sip while I still can.
Oh, right! I haven't introduced myself yet, have I?
I am Wen Tianweng, the mechanic. I am number one around here in terms of age, experience, and skills.
Unfortunately, it doesn't mean jack, because I'm the only one in the maintenance room.

I had a partner once, but he was a scoundrel. Not only did he blow a big hole in the space station, but he also kept sending back these strange letters. He always blocked the bearings and made me go repair them.
I never got along with that troublemaker. It's as if we were fated to be at odds with each other... Ah, Akivili must've turned their back on me, that's why I got stuck in there.
I was stuck for so long it was starting to ache. Ouch!
You promised to pay me...
Pay? Do I look rich to you?
I'm just a poor mechanic. I've been charged with dereliction of duty ever since that scoundrel made that giant hole in the station.
If you want a reward, I don't have any, hehe...
However! Since we've been talking this whole time and you seem agreeable enough, it's worth making an exception.
Listen carefully now. What I am going to give you is...
A hundred treasure chests?
Ten Star Rail Special Passes?
Huh... what are you on about? I am only going to show you the way to make money. You are guaranteed to make a fortune.
As for the origin of this fortune... well, it all started with this person.
Remember the scoundrel I was just talking about? His real name is <color=#dbc291ff>Hosea Lazaro</color>.

That old fart has a bunch of grand titles, like <color=#dbc291ff>former researcher in the Department of Cosmic Geography, former member of the Nameless, and member of the Armed Archaeologists</color>.

When he was still in the space station, he would boast about his inventions all day. <color=#dbc291ff>Astro Rod, Cosmos Guide chart, the Special Autoradiograph, various soft drink patents.</color> He was so arrogant and refused to obey anyone.
What's more, he would get very upset whenever he saw his colleagues from the Department of Cosmic Geography being bullied by others. He would often stand up for his colleagues and start fights.
What a scoundrel...
Humph, that's right. I am glad you can see the truth.
Sounds like a decent guy.
Yeah, right. Only impressionable young kids like you would get intimidated by those pretentious titles and inventions.
Could you get to the point?
Kids these days are always so impatient. The key to having good conversations is to let things sink in. Besides, which one of my words is not on point?
If you want the treasure, you have to listen to me talk first.
Long story short, Hosea is famous for his craftsmanship.
On one hand, it's because he likes to tinker with things in his spare time. On the other hand, it's because he would come to the maintenance room to learn from me almost every day.

He was responsible for clearing blockages. He invented Ultra Nickel Parts, and he brewed Kapo-Kali. As for me... I was responsible for supervising his work... By the way, we also wrote a book together, The Art of Soda and Space Station Maintenance.
We did have a good time... yes... it really was quite good.
Until one day, I was suddenly woken up from my sleep by a terribly loud noise —
That scoundrel blew a giant hole in the maintenance room and flew away in an aircraft! Leaving me with all the mess.
Afterward, I learned from the others that the fuel in the spacecraft that he used for his adventure was stolen bit by bit from my maintenance room!
And this is the "Station Breakout" incident that he boasts about all over the place. It's been so many years, but whenever I think about it, I'm still so mad at him.
He endured hardship to accomplish his ambition. That's so cool.
Oh come on. You think the "Station Breakout" is something to be proud of?
And that was the first time Hosea Lazaro exploited us. After that, whenever there is a tiny spark, the whole station would go up in alarm.
If you try to copy him, I guarantee that those kids from the Security Department will mop the floor with you before you even lift a foot off the ground.
That's destruction of public property. It's unforgivable.
That's right. He just wanted to cause trouble on my turf.
He just walked away, but to this very day, I am still paying the huge debt from all the damage he's done.
He betrayed his teacher and friend.
I am glad to hear you have a conscience after all! Never be like that Hosea Lazaro.
I've been told there are many young people in the Department of Cosmic Geography who worship that old scoundrel like a spiritual idol. What a bunch of buffoons.
Such a long speech. I am falling asleep...
...I went off-topic. Eh... that's what happens when you get old.

Usually, I have no one to talk to, but now that I got to let it all out, I feel much better. So, what I really want to give you is the <color=#dbc291ff>Treasure Map</color> that Hosea Lazaro left behind.
Awesome. You should have shown me earlier.
You just wanted someone to chat with, didn't you...
Of course not. Stop talking nonsense.
This thing was hidden in a corner somewhere in the space station. Someone found it and thought it was trash.
But it ended up here with me, I tried using that old scoundrel's special technique to reveal the text, and lo and behold! It revealed the coordinates of a room.
I've been told that the old scoundrel left many personal treasures in the space station. They must be hidden there.
You can look for them according to the location on the map. If you can find them, then everything belongs to you!
I have to go take a couple of sips of <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color> and tinker around with my blazing welding gun. I wouldn't give up on that even if Akivili were to come pay me a visit!
Did you find them? What are these?
Don't get me wrong. I'm just curious. I don't believe that old scoundrel would leave us anything good.
What's the paper you are holding...? Oh! That's Madam Herta... Disrespectful, really disrespectful! Give it to me and don't let others see it.
I want to keep it...
Don't be fooled! A tiger never changes its stripes. You can't trust that scoundrel Hosea.
Quick! Give it to me. If someone finds out, we are done for.
Try the Autoradiograph?
What? This treasure is also marked with the location of another treasure? What game is he playing?
Let me have a look.
What? This is an encrypted letter... the secret recipe of... <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color>!?
Why you little! Just you wait. There's enough Autoradiograph reagent—
What's he playing at, that old scoundrel.
As long as we can find the treasure.
Caramel, carbon dioxide, sounds familiar. Ambergris... Does it mean saliva!?
At least he has a shred of loyalty left. At my age, a sip of <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color> is the only thing I want...
Just forgive him already.
Enough. This is between us two old farts. Young people shouldn't get involved.
And besides, when I said I hated him, I said it in the heat of the moment.
It wasn't easy to deliver this letter.
Sorry, {F#lass}{M#lad}. I didn't expect that from him.
When I said I hated him, I said it in the heat of the moment! Argh!
Of course, I never cared about all the mess he left me with.
Ever since I was young, I have never liked academic research and dealing with the Department of Implement Arts.

My biggest wish was to hide in this maintenance room and play with the tools. Work when I wake up and sleep when I get tired. In my opinion, dealing with machines is much more fun than dealing with people...
But so many people have come and gone through this space station over the years, with the exception of Hosea.
So, I was angry that the old scoundrel didn't share his breakout plan with me. Not even a little bit.
Aren't we brothers? Shouldn't brothers be able to talk about anything?
...Nevertheless, it's been so many years. I have long since learned to let it go.
On the contrary, whenever I hear about what kind of trouble he's making outside, I really do feel happy for him.
He was born to run amok all over the cosmos.
You are very enlightened.
One has got to learn to let it go eventually.
He also thinks of you as a brother.
Maybe. But if he had really invited me to make a breakout from the space station, I may not have had the guts for it.
I like to run amok too.
You are still young. There will be plenty of opportunities in the future. Either you run amok all over the world or it runs all over you.
So, after all that... The <color=#dbc291ff>Treasure</color> is just this recipe, {F#lass}{M#lad}. What do you think?
I want to exchange it for money.

As good as the idea may sound, this manuscript is soaked in Autoradiopraph reagent, which makes it very fragile. You'll break it with the slightest touch. I'm afraid it won't last until you find a buyer.
Let me see. I guess I can give you a few treasures you won't find anywhere else. And I may have some of these ingredients in the warehouse.
You keep it, as a memento.
I do NOT want it! Unless you insist, then maybe I'll consider taking it home.
It is very important to you.
Well, in that case, let me show you something.
Let me see, these ingredients... I suppose I can find some in the warehouse if I look hard enough...
I will keep it then.
Hold on! I was just being polite. What were you thinking...?
How about this. I'll keep the manuscript, and I'll show you something else.
I want something else.
Well... then I suppose there's no other choice. That old scoundrel... after all these years, I am still paying off his debt.
Well, in that case, let me show you something.
Let me see, these ingredients... I suppose I can find some in the warehouse if I look hard enough...
Come on, a big bucket of fresh <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color>... That's the taste!
Just take these sodas with you. They can refresh your mind and strengthen your body.
{F#Lass}{M#Lad}, you're the only one who would talk to me ever since Hosea left.
If you are interested in that old scoundrel, you can look around the space station again and see if you can find some of those letters he sent back. Those letters are filled with his bragging.
That guy... just wants more people to hear his nonsense.
Old people are like that.
Nonsense can be very interesting to listen to.
Haha! You little {F#brat}{M#brat}...
Alright, enough chitchat. From now on, whenever you are free...
Ha! Just remember to come more often to chat with me.
Although I don't have much of anything here, you and I have an agreement. Whenever you pop in, there will always be enough <color=#dbc291ff>Kapo-Kali</color> for you.
To Treasure Hunters: (I)
Ah hoo! You've been fooled!
Actually, there is no treasure at all.
The only big gifts are my four graffiti drafts hidden in this room. And yes, there is also a nice picture of our respected Madam Herta. You didn't expect this, did you?
If you are a devout little researcher, take a deep breath! Don't get a heart attack!
If you are a fun-loving young person, I suggest you collect them all. Take them out when life is bad, and have some fun while studying in the dark tower.
Laughing Hosea Lazaro
To Treasure Hunters: (II)
Alright, if you can see this, it means you have followed my advice and that you possess the precious virtue of perseverance.
I must admit, you've gone such a long way. If I don't give you something, it'll be a little mean.
After all, I don't know who'd be looking for my treasure after so many Amber Eras.
There is a slim chance that maybe you are my future champion, my spiritual successor.
Wouldn't it be a pity if I accidentally hurt my friends?
Seems like there's no other way. I have to show you the real treasure now.
Your Respected Hosea Lazaro
To Treasure Hunters: (III)
Have you ever had a soda called Kapo-Kali?
It was once the signature of the space station, an anti-gravity drink extremely popular in the Southern Orion system.
Oh, sorry! Besides my other famous inventions, like the Astro Rod and Cosmos Guide, this is another one of my masterpieces.
The Interastral Peace Corporation once wanted to spend five million credits to buy its recipe, and I refused.
Wen Huairen of the Herta Department of Implement Arts has tried to steal the secret from me <unbreak>33</unbreak> times — for which he was beaten to a pulp like he deserved.
Now, I'll make it public once and for all.
It's worth five million! Please stay tuned.
Legendary Drink-Maker Hosea Lazaro
To Treasure Hunters: (IV)
Do not doubt your eyes. Above is the precious secret recipe of Kapo-Kali.
I swear on my mother's grave.
If you are one of us, you will know where to decode the password above.
Tip: A special method is required to reveal the text.
Hosea Lazaro the Terrific
This should be the room shown on the treasure map.
The treasure map revealed by a special autoradiograph is in black and white. Only the location of the target room is marked with a red circle.
(...So strange. Seems like Asta and Arlan are in trouble...)
(Still, it all sounds like hearsay to me. Better keep them in the dark for now.)
(Himeko seems to be on good terms with the folks on the space station. Maybe I should tell her first.)
Is something the matter, {NICKNAME}?
(Recount the situation in the group chat to Himeko.)
It must be difficult for Asta. Being the lead researcher isn't easy.
As soon as the Legion exits stage right, in comes the gossip... How does that saying go again? "Greet enemies outside with a smile, greet enemies inside with a sword..."
Such is the Herta company culture...
You seem pretty cheerful about it.
{NICKNAME}, are you thinking of getting involved?
No, just eating popcorn on the sidelines...
I really want to help Asta.
What do you mean? This is such an inter— Uh... inconvenient situation.
Company culture stems from the company owner...
Haha, Herta doesn't really have anything to do with it. I'm afraid wherever you find people, you find gossip of some variety.
Well, while these rumors have nothing to do with us, they do concern the reputation of young Asta. And turning a blind eye is not the way of the Nameless.

Solving a matter like this won't be difficult. Predictably, the crowd cares more about the drama than the facts. Stopping the rumors from brewing is more important right now than laying out the truth... and it's better to unearth the source of the rumors directly than to painstakingly try to refute them one by one.
As always, your guidance is wise.
You're a smooth talker, {NICKNAME}.
So we get rid of the troublemaker, right?
No, no... that's not what I meant...
I have a friend — they say there isn't a single piece of station gossip she doesn't know about.
Talking about yourself?
I didn't realize you liked gossip too, Himeko...
First of all, it's not me. Secondly, I don't make friends JUST for the sake of gossip.
It's just that my friend is pretty amazing, and I think you might be able to extract some information from her. Let's see... Right now she's probably slacking off somewhere outside the department.
I don't know her real name, but she calls herself <color=#dbc291ff>Gossipmonger</color>....
(I can't see anyone slacking off... Maybe Gossipmonger isn't around?)
(The rumors are already circulating. Let's gather some intel first.)
Have you heard anything from Gossipmonger? Is the lead researcher really that corrupt? Who exactly is this whistleblower?
Hey, aren't you off work today?
I couldn't not come in after checking my phone! Days off aren't as juicy as gossip.
Well, too bad, I haven't seen Gossipmonger this morning. You should rest up and wait for more news.
*sigh* You're right...
Why are you still here? Didn't your department call you to prepare for the emergency operation?
Uh... no? I just sneaked out for a little while. What are the odds...

I got a group message two minutes ago saying that <color=#dbc291ff>something's happened in the Special Purpose Lab — somebody's trapped</color>. The Security Department's blocked off the area around the entrance.
The Special Purpose Lab? Then wouldn't <color=#dbc291ff>Pamela — I mean, Gossipmonger be...</color>
Most likely. No wonder she's not here right now...
Gossipmonger only concerns herself with gossip, not the secrets within.
There aren't many members in the Heritor group, but news is still traveling so fast. This must be the work of something bigger...
...Hmm... Given the number of people in the group and its content... could this all stem from a few alt accounts? But why kick up a storm like this...
The walkways around the Special Purpose Lab have been temporarily closed off. Please keep your distance.
Can you let me through just this once?
I'm afraid this is a live situation. It's too dangerous.
Wait... Brother Arlan told me about you. If you insist on going... then I wish you the best of luck. Be safe.
I'm just passing through.
You're... Brother Arlan's friend!
What happened?
The Security Department received information about sightings of Legion remnants in the vicinity.
However, we just confirmed that there are monsters here that have never been seen before.
The Security Department sectioned off the area immediately, but we lost contact with some people.
Is Pamela here?
Pamela...? Let me check, I remember her name was on the rescuer list.
Did you see it? Look... It seems like the rumors about the station are true — there are Stellaron traces here.
Good luck figuring that out. All I know is that monsters have destroyed the power supply installations here.
The elevator is out of commission, so the people stuck on the floor below can't make it up.
Why don't you go down there?
It happened so suddenly. The support from the Security Department is still on the way.
We're low on staff right now — all we can do is make sure the monsters don't make it up here.
Is there anything I can do?
Maybe you can help us restart the central elevator?
There are plenty of backup power sources in the storage zone — right opposite, if I remember right.
As soon as we can restart the power supply, we can get this elevator working and rescue everyone.
Well, did you find the backup power source?
(Hand over the backup power source.)
Phew, thank goodness you're here. Give me a moment — I'll give the elevator a little shake-up.
Alright, you can use it now. Be safe.
Help! Somebody help! ...Wait, the elevator is here!
W—We lost sight of Pamela... There's a terrifying monster over there — we didn't dare to go over on our own.
Please save her! W—We'll take the elevator up.
Please!
Holy mackerel, you scared the stars out of me... Y—You took your time!
Are you Gossipmonger?
That's right, I'm the one you're looking for.
You knew I was looking for you?
Of course. Not only did I know you were coming, but I also know why.
I came to ask you something...
Heh, you want to know who Richard_Knowitall from that Heritor group is, don't you?
Heritor?
Fans of Madam Herta. They call themselves the Heritors.
I'm a businesswoman, and we play by our own rules. If you want the scoop, you have to pay the price.
I saved you, isn't that enough?
Certainly not. I have a very clear notion of how much different favors cost.
Well then, what's the price?
Don't worry, the price is a fair one. Why would I make it difficult for you?
I don't have any particular hobbies. I do indulge in a little tittle-tattling here and there, not to mention, admiring... of a certain scientist...
A—And now here you are, vanquishing monsters left, right, and center! I heard you're with the Astral Express...?
How fortunate! As it happens, I'm a huge fan of Himeko... An amalgamation of beauty and brains — the epitome of a graceful and gentle... scientist.
Soooo...?
Can you help me take a hi-def portrait photo of Himeko smiling? Pleeeaase~
Make sure you capture her electrifying smile — the one that stuns people into a trance — that million-volt smile~
This is a strange request.
What's the matter? You know Himeko well, right? If you ask her, I'm sure she'll say yes~
Alright, though it'll probably be my funeral...
I appreciate young, brave, talented people like yourself!
A superbly beautiful, dazzling, electrifying portrait shot of Himeko in exchange for the secret behind Richard_Knowitall.
Send the picture over when you have it. I'm always fair when it comes to haggling.
Did you find Gossipmonger? What did she say?
She wants your picture in exchange for information.
Ha, I knew she was weird...
You said you were friends.
*sigh* There are many types of friend... She's the type you can only stay friends with if you never meet her.
It's okay. It's just a picture. I don't mind. Go ahead, {NICKNAME}.
Let me see... Hey, you're pretty good, {NICKNAME}.
Huh? What are you taking pictures of?
Wh—What brings you here?
March 7th may have rubbed off on me.
Why do you sound so nervous all of a sudden? Suspicious...
I didn't expect to see you here. Didn't you say you were really busy?
You know what she's like. It's like nothing's happened — she's just sitting back and giving orders.
If there's time later, I want to talk to you both in more detail about this. You're the Fragmentum experts after all.
Anytime.
*sigh* I need to go — someone's taken my family encryption key. You know, the one I use to withdraw my allowance? I need to get to the bottom of it.
Someone's withholding her encryption key...
That might be the whistleblower's so-called "evidence." Looks like you don't have much time to lose, {NICKNAME}.
(A young man <color=#dbc291ff>with black-rimmed glasses and a slanted fringe</color>. Which one is Richard_Knowitall?)
And you are?
Are you Richard_Knowitall?
Richard knows what now...? What are you talking about?
Are you the one who started the rumor about Asta?
What are you talking about? When did I start rumors about the lead researcher? What nonsense.
I don't even know you. I'm gonna call security if you keep this up.
And you are?
Are you Richard_Knowitall?
Oho! Well done — you found me.
Are you the one who started the rumor about Asta?
Rumors? More like a formal complaint!
So you're here about the lead researcher's corruption? Anything for a good story, huh?
I don't get it — you people live your lives for gossip.
Wouldn't it be better to apply that drive to your research? Madam Herta would be delighted to see everyone working so hard.
I'm here to punish you.
Haha, who do you think you are? The space station's next lead researcher?
Please. Only upstanding and intelligent people like myself are worthy of such a position. You gossipers need to figure out your place in the hierarchy.
Hand over Asta's encryption key.
What encryption key...
Have you been reading too many novels? You think there's some hidden heir on this space station with keys to the family coffers? Less fantasizing, more researching, got it?
You want the scoop? Fine. I've backed it all up anyway. Here, take it. And let it be known that I, Richard_Knowitall, do not spread rumors.
This is the receipt. See the title on this purchase order...?
That's what I call substantive evidence! Hmph...
Is the source of this document reliable?
Of course it is! If I had any doubt, I'd have kept it quiet.
...I picked it up a few days ago when I was collecting a package. I saw a few receipts requiring the lead researcher's signature.
The Security Department's head honcho, Arlan — he left pretty quickly when he saw them. We all know he's on her side anyway.
So I had a peek, and woah! She's buying equipment for the space station under her own name! I've got her now!
This is no evidence at all...
Geez, do I really have to break it down for you?

The space station has its own financial procedures. As long as the purchase is for the space station, no matter how big or small, it has to go through the organizational account using the station's allocated funds.
The payer here is her private account. She's totally embezzling station funds for herself!
I'm so disappointed — so hurt! She looks like a sweet enough girl, but not only did she fail to repay Madam Herta for promoting her, she even stooped to this.
I was so angry that I was shaking. I broke out in a cold sweat!
Have you ever considered that... maybe she paid for it herself?
That amount of money? Herself!? Who do you think she is, Fleming's daughter?
Anyway, now you know everything, so leave me alone. I still need to write a report about this for Madam Herta.
(Seems like it's all just a scare...)
(But it's easy to make rumors and hard to dispel them. I better let Asta know.)
Uh, hi, how can I help you?
Are you Richard_Knowitall?
Oh, you mean the guy from the group chat — the one with the scoop?
I found out about the whole thing recently — drama for drama's sake, y'know? Don't take it too seriously...
Are you the one who started the rumor about Asta?
Started it? What do you mean? I think you have the wrong person.
I've been on overtime for the past two days — I haven't left my office...
*sigh* Sounds like a lot's happened since I last poked my head out the door...
(Doesn't fit Gossipmonger's descriptions...)
