With a couple of good meals and a good rest, he'll throw himself back into his research, or even indulge himself in a random hobby... I'm sure he'll get over it sooner or later.
No matter how bad the situation is, young people can put it behind them in a blink of an eye. Life is long, we all have to live our lives.
Some regrets will always stay in your life. Even at my age, there are regrets I can't let go of. By then, your regrets will become your life-long partner.
Everyone needs a partner...
I hope you can find a partner who's loyal to you. And I hope this partner will never become a regret in your life.
I don't want such a partner.
That is a bold idea. Unfortunately... Things don't always go the way we want.
Seems there's a story behind it.
Haha, there isn't. Don't overthink it, young one.
By the way, Rocky didn't destroy all the poems... I kept one.
He wrote this after I told him a story about a couple who was separated by time and space.
Keep it. This is a souvenir for you.
...We must stay vigilant at all times if we are to prevent any potential disasters from getting out of hand...
Excuse me?
Arlan, head of security, reporting to... Oh, it's you, {NICKNAME}. Sorry, I didn't recognize you at first.

I was just thinking about ways to improve the Security Department's emergency response training. After all, this is also an important part of Project Revival. If the Legion dares to attack us again, I don't want to make things easier for them!
Project Revival?

Well, Project Revival is a set of post-disaster operational protocols that Lady Asta and the heads of the five departments collaboratively developed, using data gathered about the damage sustained by the space station.
Wow, how proactive!
That's because I have a lot of faith in Lady Asta!

Project Revival is a set of post-disaster operational protocols that Miss Asta and the heads of the five departments collaboratively developed, using data gathered about the damage sustained by the space station.
It also involves many other confidential initiatives, such as the Curio Collection Squad, security zoning, and the Interastral Peace Corporation's damage assessment.
Curio Collection... what?
Curio Collection Squad, security zoning, and the damage assessment of Interastral Peace Corporation are all part of Project Revival.
Sounds very organized.
Well, it's all due to the clear thinking and proper planning by Lady Asta and the heads of the various departments.
But the implementation of Project Revival is not easy, and Lady Asta believes that the number of personnel needed exceeds our previous estimates.
Sorry if it seems to come out of nowhere, but {NICKNAME}, would you like to help?
You protected me in the past when we battled those Legion monsters, {NICKNAME}. You are truly a trustworthy comrade.
That's why I immediately thought of seeking your help.
It would be my honor.
Nice!
Please just order me around as you please!
This is not an "order" at all... If you are willing to help, we'd really appreciate it.

It's nothing too difficult, really. The department staff are busy with Project Revival. Can you please go to <color=#dbc291ff>every zone in the space station</color> to see if they need <color=#dbc291ff>assistance</color>?
By the way, here is your commission fee. A total of <unbreak>648</unbreak>...
I—I'm not sure how much I should offer you... Since my living expenses are all already covered by the space station, I have no idea how much money is worth.
I won't charge you anything.
Please don't turn down the offer...
We can't put a price on our friendship.
<unbreak>648</unbreak> is a huge sum of money!
Well, we shall count on you, then. I will also ask the lead researcher, Asta, to issue an access card exclusively for you.
Hopefully, with your help in Project Revival, Lady Asta will finally get a good night's sleep.
P—Please rest assured that this zone is now completely under the con—control of the Curio Collection Squad!
Why is your voice shaking?
Shaking? It i—is not. You must've misheard.
Phew, phew... Calm down, Abraham. As a member of the Curio Collection Squad, you must always stay calm.
Fear, if picked up by others, will not only make everyone distrust you, but also ruin your chance to avenge Alfred.
I remember you. You are that guy who is morbidly scared of death.
Remember me? I—I also remember you... But now I'm not a—afraid of death anymore...
The friends who had once stood by my side day and night have already taken the lead in entering the eternal night, and yet I'm still here, not knowing when my life will end.
Life is but a path to death, but not today.
I don't want to die at the hands of those monsters until I avenge Alfred!
Mrs. Hinkel transferred me here from the Obstacle Detection Terminal so that I could follow the lead of Wen Mingde, head of the Curio Collection Squad, to toughen myself up on the front line.
But as soon as I came here, I encountered a problem about, about...
Reactivating the Space Anchor over there!
That's too hard.
You think so too!? Great, I'm not alone.
Even I can do it.
Don't put it like that... You are the big hero who saved the space station. This's not something that anyone can do. You are being too modest...
The solution is just a few steps away!
It may look like a few steps, but I can't do it, even if I muster all my courage...
Well, actually, the activation itself isn't the difficult part. You just need to get close to the Space Anchor, and the biological polarity of your body will be enough to activate it.
The real challenge is all the monsters along the way.
Back when I was working at the Obstacle Detection Terminal, they were nothing but distant shadows that I could just brush aside.
Then the invasion happened. And when I learned that they got Alfred, my heart began to fill up with hatred.
But when I became a member of the Curio Collection Squad and met them face to face, all I felt was fear!
At that moment, Alfred's fading eyes flashed in my head. I felt short of breath, with cold sweat all over my body and my legs trembling...
What a loser, right? I just couldn't find the courage to go through with it and activate the Space Anchor. And it had been like this for several days...
So, {NICKNAME}, do you think you can...
Leave it to me!
I really admire you. Your perserverance and courage in the face of death have inspired me.
I'm well aware of my limitations, so I'll just wait here for an update from you.
Let's go together. We can look out for each other.
N—N—No, I can't. I'll just get in the way...
{NICKNAME}, please <color=#dbc291ff>activate the Space Anchor</color>. I am counting on you!
L—L—Left, The Hunt...
The Hunt on the left, Harmony on the right, and Erudition in the heart...
It's done.
I can hear something... but no matter what happens, even if I die the next second, I must finish reciting this phrase.
The Hunt on the left, Harmony on the right, Erudition in the heart, and Preservation on the chest!
Okay, well done, Abraham.
Wow, you are back already? I only recited this morale chant <unbreak>167</unbreak> times, and the Space Anchor is already activated.
What are you doing?
Hey, you're back already! So soon! I've only recited this morale chant <unbreak>167</unbreak> times.
Before you say anything, please allow me to finish reciting it, otherwise, I will feel very uncomfortable.
I understand!
Thank you, you're very kind.
Well, hurry up...
Yes, I am going as fast as I can.
The Hunt on the left, Harmony on the right, Erudition in the heart, and Preservation on the chest!
Phew... Okay. Well done, Abraham.
Now, let's get back to business. I see that the Space Anchor over there has been reactivated.
The dragon on your chest!
On the chest is Preservation!
This is the chant of Aeon protection that I came up with myself. Please don't alter the wording, lest we offend the Aeons.
But I only recited this chant <unbreak>167</unbreak> times and you already activated the Space Anchor.

Actually, when I was reciting the chant, I figured it all out... Since you've helped me complete my task already, I can now continue to stay on the team. And I will eventually hunt down the monster that killed Alfred and avenge him.
I will prove to you that I have the courage to take that step before the long night of death.
I hope this is not our last encounter. Farewell, {NICKNAME}...
How come you never have anything good for me?
Huh? Isn't this a good thing?
With this, <color=#dbc291ff>you can travel between the various zones with ease</color>, except for certain hidden places.
...What is this? "Battle of intellects is a source of pride. Physical exertion brings shame"? It's complete nonsense! So physical labor doesn't count as work now?
Today, I'm gonna show them all what real work is about!
S—Sorry.
Yep, show them!
Hear! Hear!
All staff present, attention please — Herta Space Station is undergoing a difficult period of revival.
In the battle with the Legion, some of our colleagues were slaughtered by monsters, and their cold bodies were thrown into the silent space.
The cyber attack has erased years of research efforts. The damaged Curios are slowly disintegrating in a weightless environment.
Everything within sight has been turned into a wasteland, and monsters are still roaming around in our cabins.
No matter how many dazzling achievements you have made on your own, we can no longer afford to live like hermits.
We need to mobilize every member of our staff, put down our inherent prejudices, and work together to recover the lost Curios and repair the damaged cabins.
So inspiring!
So lame...
Silence! If any staff member feels unhappy with this, please air your grievances to me face to face.
I'm all ears.
If you don't mind, I don't want to hear any more complaints about physical labor, nor do I want to see anyone putting off work.
If you are interested in Curio recovery, please report to the Curio Collection Squad under Mr. Wen Mingde in the base zone as soon as possible.
Those who are interested in repair work, come to me now to learn the process.
I can help with the repairs.
Good, good. Are you the young {M#man}{F#lady} who helped out in the master control zone? I have a special task for you.
Does everyone have to participate?
Every staff member must take responsibility sooner or later. The space station is now in dire need of restoration. I believe we can use everyone's help.
I remember you. You are the young {M#man}{F#lady} who helped out in the master control zone. Great. I have a special task for you.
<unbreak>45</unbreak> meters out the door from where we are now, there is a major road defect.
I've checked, and the small ordnance depot on the other side of the defect is swarming with monsters. I'm afraid ordinary staff won't be able to deal with this.
Don't worry. Just leave it to me.
Looks like I am the only one...
Yes, <color=#dbc291ff>make sure to repair the road and eliminate the monsters at the end of it.</color>
I have many other matters to attend to. Please report back to me when you finish the task.
{F#Young lady}{M#Young man}, you're back. Let me concentrate and inspect your work.
There is a <unbreak>0.5</unbreak> ms time delay between the sound reaching both ears, which indicates that the source is in the 3 or 9 o'clock position.
The sound is much louder in the left ear, which confirms the 9 o'clock position. That means the monsters in the 3 o'clock position have been eliminated. Good job.
Such an incredible skill!
It's just sonar positioning. Nothing to brag about.
In the Herta Department of Ecology, we deal with all sorts of cosmic creatures every day. Developing this kind of ability is just part of our training.
The staff of Herta Space Station possess many different abilities. After meeting a few of us, you won't be surprised anymore.
I can't hear anything.
You're untrained. It's normal that you can't hear anything. This is a sonar positioning technique that is unique to the space station's Ecology staff.
In the Herta Department of Ecology, we deal with all sorts of cosmic creatures every day. Developing this kind of ability is just part of our training.
The staff of Herta Space Station possess many different abilities. After meeting a few of us, you won't be surprised anymore.
Why don't you just take a look...
Hehe, you have a point.
I should also reflect on whether I, like so many others, have fallen into the trap of overreliance on Erudition and disregarding the much simpler and perhaps more effective methods.
In short, thank you for your contribution to Herta Space Station. This is the reward I managed to secure for you from Lead Researcher Asta. Please take it.
Thank you. You seem to care a lot about this place.
No need to reward me for such a minor good deed.
I disagree. All these minor acts of kindness are precisely what make the reconstruction possible.
Back when I was an unknown researcher, I was told by the first group of people who worked on the construction of Herta Space Station, "This universe is never friendly. Rather, it is vast and dark."
In this vast universe, there are countless pairs of eyes staring at the space station, with various intentions.
Some covet its Curios, while others envy its neutrality and freedom.
Others despise it or see it as a chess piece that can be destroyed and trampled on at will.
Perhaps we researchers are the only ones who understand the joy, sadness, epiphany, and companionship that it has brought us.
Which is why it is up to us to give everything we have to protect it.
Mr. Wen, excuse me...
...Who? Who is interrupting me? If it is the <color=#dbc291ff>Xenohydro</color>, then show yourself at once!
Ahem, so it's you, {NICKNAME}. You're also here to volunteer in the Curio Collection Squad... Wait, don't come over here!
Just say one or two words.
I'm not kidding. You have to say one and two.
One.
One, two.
Ahahaha.
You don't have to laugh like that.
One.
Ahahaha.
You don't have to laugh like that.
... No abnormal watery sound in your pronunciation. Pupillary reflex normal, perspiration reaction normal.
Okay, now you can come over and let me touch your forehead—

The <color=#dbc291ff>Xenohydro</color> can't achieve this level of likeness... Alas, the lead was once again inconclusive. Even if the recollection of Curios is the top priority in the Declaration of Revival, it is proving to be a difficult task in practice.
Xenohydro?

As you know, since the establishment of the Herta Space Station, five departments have been established to focus on the collection and study of Curios, including <color=#dbc291ff>Ecology, Geopolitics, Mysticism, Geography, and Implement Arts</color>.
This monster invasion caused the loss of roughly half of the hundreds of collections held by each department.

They come in all kinds of sizes and shapes. Some are inactive and harmless, some emit poison for no reason, not to mention some biological types of Curios that can plan their own escape, which is a real headache.

There is a Curio called the <color=#dbc291ff>Xenohydro</color> that has the ability to replicate the appearance of other people at will. This allows it to wreak havoc and confusion wherever it goes, as it can easily assume various false identities.
Curio Collection?
The Curio Collection Squad is an emergency team I put together. The team's mission is to support post-disaster reconstruction and ensure that all of its needs are met during this difficult time.
As the name suggests, it is mainly responsible for collecting the Curios that have been displaced due to the recent monster invasion.
Declaration of Revival?
Surely, you must have heard of Mrs. Hinkel's famous Declaration of Revival, right?
"Our fellow researchers were slaughtered by monsters. Their lifeless forms were cold and woeful..."
Woeful...
Alas, I can't recall the exact wording. After all, Mrs. Hinkel's style is unique and not easily imitable.
Well, you truly are a man of dedication, Mr. Wen.
*sigh* It's all because of that Xenohydro's trickery. This has been tormenting me to no end! That's why we had to have that conversation earlier.

The squad has been searching for the Xenohydro for some time, but to no avail. A member of the squad named <color=#dbc291ff>Abraham</color> has even gone missing... It is true what they say — when it rains, it pours.
Missing? I can help with this.
That's great. I was just getting worried that I can't spare anyone to go find him.
Abraham is easy to identify. He is thin, wearing glasses, and always mumbling about "Life is but a path to death."
You don't even pay attention to how he looks. You can just take a moment to listen to the words being said. He somehow always manages to drop this line at least once every five sentences.
Is it the Abraham I know?
Oh, you know him? He was recently transferred to this squad from Mrs. Hinkel's, always mumbling about...
Life is but a path to death.
That's right! He says this at least once out of every five sentences.
According to the squad members, Abraham was last seen in the storage zone.
*sigh* Even though Abraham can be quite the downer, which has been a real torture for his colleagues...
Still we can't just leave him.
I can't stand him either.
But we can't just leave him.

Right now, all squad members are busy searching for missing Curios. And I'll also have to handle the whole <color=#dbc291ff>Xenohydro</color> situation. So it's all up to you to find <color=#dbc291ff>Abraham</color>.
If you bring him back safely, the Department of Implement Arts will reward you quite handsomely.
T—Today I'm going to get justice for Alfred!
Whoa, whoa — don't come near me, go away—
Help!
Help! Help me!
They're everywhere—
Darn it! I can't believe I actually bought that Asta girl's nonsense about how the station is on a hiring spree!
No one's even watching the blockade, and now my old butt is blocked here too.
Darn the kids these days. They only know how to rattle my old bones...
Aaaah.
The {F#lass}{M#lad} over there, hello!
What's the matter?
What's the matter? Don't you see I'm stuck here? Young people these days. Your brain's fried, and your eyes ain't no good either.
I — can't — hear — you!
Oh my gosh, the kids these days. Have you lost your hearing? At such a young age? Then take a look with your eyes. I'm stuck!

If you ask me, I'd say this shouldn't have happened. There should always be two people dealing with bearing blockages, one up top and one at the bottom, in case of repulsion bridge failures. But who could've guessed that none of the kids these days are willing to do this job now?
{F#Lass}{M#Lad}, the control device of the repulsion bridge is right opposite me. Take the elevator and reset it to let me come over, and then you can get out of here.
I'll be right there.
Hurry up. I won't let you go empty-handed.
How much will you pay me?
Gee, kids these days, all you know is money.
I don't want your money.
So it's not enough then. Fine, use your imagination, I will pay you whatever you want.
One hundred!
Ten thousand!
A hundred million!
Agreed!
Good {F#lass}{M#boy}! If you operate on the control device over there, you can come to me... Cough, cough.
I've been trapped here all day. I'm hungry, thirsty, and running out of oxygen. I don't have the strength to speak. I have to reserve energy.
So, you've got some pretty quick moves. There are lots of nice things here. Help yourself. I got other things to attend to. Bye.
Where's my reward?
That's it?
Don't try to fool me.
Come on, get out of the way, I can't hold it anymore. Come get me in the maintenance room if you need anything!
One, two, three...
One, two, three...
Are you exercising?
You're responsible for all these archives?
♪ One, two, three, one, two, three, drink... ♪
Three. You see?
Three are missing.
Gotta find these videotapes.

I know I am right about this. I may be getting old. I may have forgotten all about the Aeons... but I keep track of the number of these tapes like my life depends on it. Kid, you came just in time. If you have time, go find them for me.
If you don't, then I suppose I'll have to get help from those old farts.
Old farts?

Yeah. There's Wen Tianweng, who talks to machine parts all day in the maintenance room. Bernard in the Department of Cosmic Geography who gives nicknames to the scrolls and plants. And there's Gunn, who can lie through his teeth without a blink of an eye.
Yep, there's an old fart suited to every job.
Videotapes?

The videotapes in the space station are different from ordinary ones. They are recordings of <color=#dbc291ff>wonders and mysteries</color> you won't find anywhere. Because of this, they need to be looked after by specialized personnel.
This is a great learning opportunity for you. You should count yourself lucky.
Let's not trouble those old fa... elderly people.
Good, good. We don't see many accommodating young fellows like you nowadays.
However, I have to remind you that the producers of these videotapes have implanted some defense mechanisms to help protect their secrets.

If you are not careful when touching the videotapes, best-case scenario is you will feel a little dizzy, and the data transfer may be forcibly interrupted. Worst-case scenario, it may cause abnormal behaviors, hallucination, and paranoia, eventually leading to memory and consciousness disorders.
Good thing I'm not interested in secrets.
In this bizarre space station, sometimes even if you cover your eyes and ears, the information destined for you will still find a way into your brain.
Secrets choose their witnesses — this is a fundamental belief of the Department of Insight.
"It's A Trap!"

Not so much of a trap. It's just a result of the constant arms race between researchers vying to be the best at what they do. They simply used a certain kind of technology to turn away those deemed unworthy from accessing information.
Malicious baits are deeply embedded in the information by means of flashing visual stimuli and inaudible ultrasound waves, thus manipulating the subconscious to inflict harm on the subject.

Consciousness, preconsciousness, and subconsciousness; self, ego, and superego; imagination, symbolism, reality, and so on. The labyrinth of the human mind is a compulsory subject that almost all space station researchers are proficient in.
Is it too late for me to refuse now?
Stop being coy with me. I have met a lot of people in my life. You don't seem to be the kind who would refuse secrets.
If I tell you not to think about an elephant — then images of the large gray animal must be all over your mind.
And now I've told you everything about the videotapes — you won't easily forget about the danger until you find out the secrets.
I am guessing someone took advantage of the Legion's invasion and snatched the videotapes when the master control zone was unguarded.

There are no borrowing records, indicating that the suspect is unwilling to expose their identity. There was no sign of damage, indicating that they were not trying to destroy those videotapes but to view the secret within.
The device for playing those videotapes is located in the <color=#dbc291ff>safe area of the supply zone</color>. If you go there, you may find some clues.
Videotape: Dim Blue Dot
You stare at the empty screen. The faint fluorescent light seems ready to begin its dangerous display. Sensing your approach, lines of gold and purple flash rapidly on the screen.
Watch the video.

The point of view appears to be falling into empty space without beginning or end. The camera eventually gets focused — now you're looking at the vast hinterland of the universe through a standard-issue navigation visor. In the distance is a bright blue dot, like a condensed water droplet. You recognize it as the Herta Space Station.

The next second, crystallized cracks spread silently across the screen. The dim blue flickers, monsters spread all over the sky, and the silent planet begins to crack slowly apart. Then comes the flash back, from a baby crying in the cradle, to the joyous laughter and the resentment in teenage years, and the space station's cold reflection before the final departure.

They say your life flashes before your eyes at the final moment of your life. This video undoubtedly records the last moments of a deceased person's life. You struggle to pull yourself out of the immersive dark mud. All you hear is the intermittent cosmic radio...
It seems to be calling a name you cannot hear clearly.
This trip feels dangerous...
It is still calling the name you cannot hear clearly.
It's amazing, like watching someone's memory.
It is still calling the name you cannot hear clearly.
Take out the videotape.
Videotape: Justice

You stare at the empty screen. The faint fluorescent light seems ready to begin its dangerous display. Sensing your approach, there was an indescribable rustle that sounded off from the surrounding distance, enough to run a chill down your spine.
Watch the video.

The camera centers on the white table in a conference room and begins to shake slowly. The scene is dense and noisy. Then a majestic voice starts reading a report about the establishment of the Herta Department of Galactic Geopolitics.
The voice says that when the will of the Aeons is regarded as the standard, the will of man will withdraw from history accordingly.
The problem is that our world favors the Aeons, who can reap power from their Paths. Here, the strong get to make the rules and power defines justice.

What the Department of Galactic Geopolitics wants to oppose is this status quo of the strong ruling over the weak. Those rights and interests ignored by the Aeons will be upheld by us. Those who are trampled will receive our help.
We are committed to rebuilding the value of justice for humans in the cosmos. This is the proposal of the two founders, Gunn Konolev and Sheila Nova.

Before the voice finishes, there is already applause and jeers in the Conference Room. So they are the Konolevs of the Department of Galactic Geopolitics! During this passionate event, you see countless handshakes in front of the camera until you hear someone call out a name.

"Sheila!" A powerful voice calls out, accompanied by background noises that are hard to separate from it, as if inextricably intertwined. This is the most direct proof of Aeonic powers: In the face of the destruction of the planet, the justice sought by men is laughably insignificant. While you struggle to distinguish the name Sheila, you are drowned out by the murmurs in the background.
The end of the video seems to be blurry.
Suddenly, you get a splitting headache, forcing you to give up the thought.
Those two geopolitics researchers sound familiar.
Suddenly, you get a splitting headache, forcing you to give up the thought.
Take out the videotape.
Videotape: Doomsday
You stare at the empty screen. The faint fluorescent light seems ready to begin its dangerous display. You wait quietly for a while, but nothing happens.
Watch the video.

The screen lights up. The supply zone is wide open, but the spacecraft is still under control. The faint glimmers from neutrino explosions stain the platform a shade of yellow. In the disturbing silence, you hear increasingly rapid breathing...

Breathe. Run. Open the hatch, lock the navigation interface and move on to the next one. Until you are stopped by a pair of hands. They belong to... a young geopolitics researcher with eyes like an eagle's.
Eagle Castle has been destroyed, he says. This is the most direct proof of the power of the Aeons: In the face of the destruction of the planet, the justice sought by men is laughably insignificant.
He lowers his voice. "Now that the cosmic route is blocked by that thing... There's no chance you can rush back to your home planet to sound the alarm before the Antimatter Legion arrives."
If you do that, you will be intercepted along the way by some evil monster with nothing but the desire to destroy. Promise me, don't go back to die. Stay here, continue our research.
The next second, the researcher is pushed aside and an intact aircraft can be seen behind him. Amidst the noise of the lift-off, you hear the geopolitics researcher shout out a name, as though...

As though you have heard it before on the radio. "Sorry," a tired voice comes through from the noisy radio. "The space station chose to remain neutral in the invasion by the Legion. No reinforcements will arrive. If you can, please return as soon as possible according to the scheduled route. Do you hear me?"
It seems this is not the first time the Legion played the bad guys.
Intermittently, a name is repeated on the cosmic radio. No answer.
A researcher once left the space station with information.
Intermittently, a name is repeated on the cosmic radio. No answer.
Take out the videotape.
These videotapes seem to be related... they seem to be records of different stages of life of the same person.
A <color=#eb4d3dff>space radio</color> called Sheila <color=#eb4d3dff>pursued justice</color> for <color=#eb4d3dff>a doomed planet</color> geopolitics researcher.
The sentences in your mind suddenly become broken and disordered. In your vision, the dark cabin gradually becomes distorted and strange.
You get a splitting headache and then lose consciousness.
Come with me.
This is...
The medical cabin of Herta Space Station.
You fainted because of contact with improper information. Can you tell me what information you have been exposed to?
The life of a deceased...
The life of a geopolitics researcher.
The life of someone who fought against the Legion...
(Also the life of a person named Sheila...)
Whatever it is, I have cleared the mental contamination for you. Now, you'd better <color=#dbc291ff>go for a walk</color>, and see if you have any other symptoms.
Emergency resolved, now let's continue — same problem this time?
Well, I seem to keep... forgetting things lately.
I have told you many times before that it is very normal to forget things sometimes.
No, I've been forgetting basic things. Like, my birthday, who my friends are. Or how I came to the space station.
Fine. Just to reassure you, I will give you a full-body scan using the capsule treatment module this time. There's nothing wrong with your physical functions.

On the contrary, they're a little... too perfect. Of course, that's your gift. After all, having a talent is not an unusual occurrence, and your talent seems to be your physical health. So, in turn, it's only fair that you might have a poor memory.
With such a perfect physical condition, I better keep this on file. Let me make a record of this. What's your name?
Oh, yes, Dr. Joanne. My name is...
Sheila Nova.
Well, look at you, newcomer. You're so agile. You can easily escape from any monster raid.
(Sheila Nova... That's the name mentioned in the video.)
(In the video recording, she clearly left the space station. She even... died.)
(There must be something to this. It also matches the secret Esther was talking about.)
(I should investigate this so-called Sheila first.)
Don't wander around. You are affected by those videotapes, the consciousness disorder you're experiencing is no joke. This is the price you pay for being nosy.
Is there any way to alleviate the symptoms?
Thanks to the kindness of Abundance, there are panaceas that can cure all diseases scattered around the medical cabin. You can try using them.
I can't guarantee anything, but at least... They're a little better than placebos.
No, Joanne, it's definitely not ordinary forgetfulness. It's like someone stole my memories overnight...
Maybe you had a run-in with a Memosnatcher.

Are you talking about those radicals in the Garden of Recollection? There's nothing those guys wouldn't do to get hold of other people's memories. If this is their doing, ordinary treatment is not going to work.

So, what next?
Hehe, I've got a backup plan.
The memetic virus is transmitted through virtual data. And all the virtual data in the space station leave traces in the terminal.
Since we couldn't get much from our previous investigation, let's check the browsing records of the three suspects. Then we should be able to identify the source of the infection.
Hehe, I've got an emergency plan for situations like this. Please visit the Data Exchange Center — where the terminal is located.
But I've never used a terminal...
Don't worry. It's simple. Enter the terminal room, verify your identity, and you can start your query.
Why don't you go yourself?
*sigh* I have my own reasons. It's a long story.

Simply put, anyone using any data gadget, which basically includes everyone on the space station, would have their user behaviors recorded by the terminal. It is thus inappropriate for me or any other staff member to check such information.
Um, I still don't get it.
Don't worry. I'll explain to you when I have time.
I know. You are just looking for excuses to slack off.
It's not like that. I would have gone if I could.
Think about it. Despite different backgrounds and identities, people on the space station have reached an agreement on personal privacy.
The traces left from using virtual data can be found on the terminal. For example, from here people can see all the unusual virtual platforms you visited during your working hours.
Therefore, to respect everyone's privacy, no one, including myself and the other staff, should access the terminal.
Think about it in their shoes, if you are space station staff, would you be happy with me going through your browsing records on the virtual network?
I'd rather die...
It's unacceptable.
Now you understand, right? That's why your special identity makes you the perfect candidate for this!
Why? I don't understand.
Let me start with your heroic deeds and your special identity.
So, you just want me to get beaten up?
Jeez, is this the kind of nonsense you think about all day? I have nothing against you. Why would I set you up?
From an objective point of view, you are an outsider on the space station. You are not familiar with most people here, so it's unlikely that you hold any personal grudge against anyone.
Not every outsider has the right to access the data records. But you are different. You are the hero who saved the space station. People trust your moral character.
But of course, if you do decide to help, I hope you will keep everything you see strictly confidential.
No problem. My lips are sealed.
Anyway, keep it all a secret while you're still in the space station. As for where you go or what you do in the future, it's none of my business.
Piece of cake. Just leave it to me.
Thank you so much!
Before you leave, let me tell you how to use the terminal.
As you know, the invasion of the station severely damaged the whole data center. And the server room where the terminal is housed is no exception.

Despite our best efforts, the damage is yet to be fully remediated. And reported cases of memetic virus infection only made things worse. I had to send a maintenance engineer to monitor the situation on a daily basis.

<color=#dbc291ff>The engineer would turn on the optical identity verification program manually every day</color> to check whether the bioelectricity of each visitor entering the room is normal, thus ensuring that the terminal room is not invaded.
Since the optical identity verification program is <color=#dbc291ff>refreshed dynamically after it is turned on every day, you need to re-verify your identity every time you enter.</color>
For more details, please <color=#dbc291ff>consult the maintenance engineer</color>. I've told the engineer that you have permission to enter the room.
So... I will leave the rest to you!
A row of large words pops up on the terminal screen: <color=#eb4d3dff>"Code error <unbreak>505</unbreak>: Service unavailable."</color>
There are no other responses.
Someone runs back into the room, panting. Looks like he's the <color=#dbc291ff>"maintenance engineer"</color> Asta mentioned.
The terminal doesn't respond. Let me ask him.
Sorry — huff puff — I'm sorry!
Are you {NICKNAME}? Asta already gave me a heads up that you are going to come use the terminal.
I'm terribly sorry. The computer system in the next room suddenly initiated an auto-update. The researchers didn't have time to save their results. So I went to help them just now.
The terminal did not respond.
Prompted error code <unbreak>505</unbreak>?
Ahh, I didn't connect the data to the terminal while I was away. Let me turn it on. It'll just take a second...
It's all set now! Please verify your identity again. And the results will come up when you input your query.
(It turns out Mare had been suffering from insomnia. Now she can fall asleep after watching short videos of cats snoring.)
(So she was just imitating the sound of cats last time.)
(Turns out she's just a run-of-the-mill cat lover. That's all good. She can't be the one who got infected.)
(Let me check the other people's records...)
A row of large words pops up on the terminal screen: <color=#eb4d3dff>"Insufficient computing power. Please try again later."</color>
After several attempts, the same message still keeps popping up. Perhaps the terminal meant "a lot later."
I'd better ask the <color=#dbc291ff>maintenance engineer</color> to fix it.
What's wrong?
I only found one record.
Good... Oh, you mean you couldn't find the others?
"Insufficient computing power. Try again later?"
Oh, that's normal. The terminal is not broken. It's nothing to worry about.
Although, it won't be operational until tomorrow.
Why?
Because the station was invaded. Originally, we had more than one terminal, connecting units on a much larger scale.
During that debacle, some units were damaged. The computing power of the terminal was thus greatly decreased, not to mention it's only running on a single-core processor right now...
The lead researcher said she was going to purchase new equipment. But it hasn't arrived yet. Therefore, with the current computing power, you can only query once a day.

And the current identity verification program has to be activated manually by me every day, so... please <color=#dbc291ff>come back tomorrow</color>. Don't forget to ask me to turn on the verification.
Here you are!
Please turn on the terminal for me.
Yup, here you go! The optical identity verification program has been set up. The terminal has sufficient computing power. Please feel free to use it.
(People act much more maliciously on the virtual network. He was brutally harassed online. Did he get infected by the memetic virus during his most vulnerable moments?)
(But his speech and the style of his posts are significantly different from the "cliché quotes" Asta had mentioned. I'm afraid he's not the infected one.)
(Then is it Joanne? But I better not jump to a conclusion just yet. I should check Joanne's records.)
A row of large words pops up on the terminal screen: <color=#eb4d3dff>"Query failed. Click to refresh."</color>
However, no matter how many times you click, the same message still pops up. I better ask the maintenance engineer.
What? Is it broken again?
It kept asking me to refresh...
It seems to be some compatibility issues...
Broken "again?"
Well, it sometimes breaks down during maintenance.
Oh no! This is caused by the old units I installed into the terminal today. They looked good to me at the time and I thought they could boost the terminal's computing power.
Looks like we'll have to wait until the replacement units are delivered.
Sorry, please give me some time. Let me remove these units. I assure you the existing computing power won't be affected.
However, I'm afraid you'll have to <color=#dbc291ff>come back tomorrow</color>. I'm sure by tomorrow there will have been sufficient computing power!
We've got enough computing power today. I've reported it to the lead researcher. She said she expects you to get this done today.
Please let me know when you are done. I'll need to reinforce the terminal's security system.
Sure. Please turn on the terminal for me.
The optical identity verification program is all set. The terminal has sufficient computing power. Please help yourself!
(I understand every single word but I don't understand when they are put together. I feel dizzy reading them. I want to throw up...)
(...What on earth justifies my continued existence in this world? If a person is without any career, would they be any different from a piece of space garbage...)
(Hold on. What was I thinking? That was close! I almost got infected by the memetic virus!)
(From Joanne's record, it is clear that this memetic virus interferes with one's mind and manipulates people into a pointless rat race. This virus is truly vicious!)
(I should head back. But before I go, I better tell the engineer. After all, I promised him...)
Are you done?
Yes, I think I got the result.
Okay. According to the space station data center's regulations, your query access will be terminated as soon as you leave the terminal room. Thank you for your cooperation.
I've gone through all the data records.
Great. I heard from the maintenance engineer that, due to incomplete recovery from the previous invasion, the terminal's computing power had been hindering your progress.
So I didn't expect you to finish the investigation so soon. Thank you for your hard work. So what's the conclusion?
(Tell her your observation and your analysis.)
Haha, I see. I did have a suspicion that Joanne was the one who got infected. But I didn't have any substantial evidence.
How did you know it was her?
Simple. Out of the three of them, she is the only one who exhibited speech patterns similar to those of the Crackup Conch after its infection.
I've always found it rather suspicious that she, a person who dozes off all the time, would have such a drastic change of personality and would quit all her habits and hobbies out of nowhere.
Have you ever suspected the other two?
Their behaviors may seem strange to you, but to me, they are extremely normal.
Let's start with Mare. Getting distracted at work is such a common occurrence for all humans. It sometimes happens to me, even when I'm working in my favorite field of research.

Then there's Chris. He is said to be a good student from a poor family. And compared with the other researchers, he's still fairly new here on the space station. So it's normal that he would experience discomfort after a lengthy space flight.
What surprised me was the severity of his discomfort. So I've already sent for a doctor to check on him.
Anyway, the overall result is as expected. Next, we should weed out Joanne's virus and get her "back on track" to her old self.
Thank you for your hard work on finding such substantial evidence, so—
Hold on, I have a few questions.
Oh? Go ahead. I'll answer all your questions if I know the answers.
I still don't get it...
Huh?
Is there anything else I need to clarify?
Isn't it a good thing to keep Joanne this way?
...That was a dangerous thought. Of course not. Joanne is a living human being. You shouldn't think like that.
Although we come from different cultural backgrounds, some of the most basic rights and interests are recognized by all of us as the common bottom line and must not be deprived.
Besides, based on my personal experience, you'll never get great results in any field of research unless you are passionate about it.
How did you guess correctly that Joanne was the one?
Guess? I didn't "guess." To some extent, it was just simple psychology.

Joanne completely wiped out her personal life, which is very unusual. Think about this simple analogy. People's capacity for work is limited, just like how a balloon can only hold a finite amount of air...
When they don't get enough rest or fulfillment, people will just be like a balloon being unceasingly inflated, which will inevitably blow up if there's no chance for an air release.
Aren't you worried about the other two?
Worried about what? Do you mean how their research at the space station will be affected? I don't think there's any problem except that Chris might need some psychological counseling from a doctor.
People have the freedom to do whatever they want in their own lives, as long as they don't undermine the security of the space station or violate the regulations.
I don't have any more questions.

Well, I do get your point to some extent. It might seem productive, at least in the short term, to just disregard people's safety concerns and force them into nonstop work. But in the real world, such practices will only spell disaster.
The station is built in space, far away from any land surface. Not everyone can adapt to life here. This will become clear after a while.
Despite our top-notch equipment and resources, some people still find it unbearable to live on the station after staying here for a long time.

In that case, letting people develop their own hobbies improves everyone's mental health, especially when they have been away from land for an extended period of time. This is the best way to improve overall productivity.
After all, we are born to be humans, not plants or rocks that do not have emotions. How could we still call ourselves humans if we were to throw away our hobbies and emotions?
But I don't seem to have any hobbies...
Well, I do know a little about your situation. It's alright. You still have a long way to go. You'll eventually find your hobbies and your own way of life.
That makes sense.
Of course it does. This is also my life experience. Having fun in life is all about investing in things that you find interesting.
Well, you still have a long way ahead of you. When you are out there exploring, remember — no matter what, don't just throw away your hobbies and your emotions.
Oh right, by the way, I almost forgot one thing.
I know paper records will be printed out at the terminal. Keep those records to yourself. Don't let the information leak out in the space station. Promise me, or I'll take back the reward.
Don't worry, they will never leak out.
Well, anyway, thank you so much. This is the reward for you. I made this myself.
Ehem, if you don't like it, I can take you to buy the starnought fleet when the latest version comes out. It's very popular among young people these days.
Jarilo-VI, we're here.
Brrr. It really is one big snowball.
It really is one big snowball.
Hey, get your own metaphor!
It doesn't feel that cold.
Well the Trailblaze Path grants us faint power. It allows us to better adapt to harsh environments.
*sigh* Snow as far as the eye can see. Which direction should we take?
Based on the coordinates, the target should be up ahead.
Then what are we waiting for? Let's go.
Why didn't we land at the destination?
...Do you want to mention the time we smashed a hole through Taikiyan Stadium, or shall I?
*sigh* Please stop bringing that up. Let's just say that landings and crowds don't mix.
Unless you enjoy trailblazing through two weeks of community service.
I said drop it!
I didn't know we'd be hiking...
Me neither, if only we had a snowmobile... We never get to bring anything cool from the Express.
Do you remember what you did to our last snowmobile?
...Anyway, moving on.
Remember, we should stay vigilant. We know very little about this world.
Calm down. Between the three of us, nothing will stand in our way.

I mean c'mon, {NICKNAME}, you've got a Stellaron in your body, I have my special {RUBY_B#Mysterious Ice Crystal}Six-Phased Ice{RUBY_E#} powers, and Dan Heng... Uhh, he's got that mysterious past thing going for him...
So, if people start creating trouble for us, they're gonna regret it!
Yeah, they're gonna regret it!
...So how long does "copycatitis" last?
Let's just make sure that we're not the ones creating trouble...
Well, let's not get ahead of ourselves, hehe...
Let's go. Braving the unknown... that's the real spirit of trailblazing!
...Hey, get outta there or you'll shiver to death.
Holding your breath won't help...
I got this, March.
If someone's got their head stuck in the sand, or the snow in this case...
...they just need a helping hand.
Yeowch!
My fine fellow, was that really necessary? Is crawling around in the snow a crime these days? I mean, c'mon, surely it doesn't warrant a spearing?
...But then again how can I blame you? I mean, I caught you off guard. It had to happen — you could even say I deserved it, huh? Besides, I've made a gallant group of new friends as a result, hehe...
...Is Captain Gepard around? H—He's an old buddy of mine...
Who?
Wait, you're not Silvermane Guards? Well, why didn't you say so? Turns out we're on the same side after all!
Pleasure to meet you, the name's Sampo Koski.
I'm {NICKNAME}.

Excellent, I'll remember the name. I never thought I'd run into friends from the same line of work out here in this frozen wasteland. *sigh* Business is bad these days, but fear not, Sampo Koski isn't interested in hoarding. There's more than enough treasure to go around, so let's get rich together! Hahaha.
Say, why don't we join forces? I have reliable intel the main strength of the Silvermane Guards is being deployed to the front line. This is a golden opportunity...
What business are you talking about?
Silvermane Guards?
The front line?
...Come now, friends. I can understand the mistrust, but there's no need for the charade.
Then again, I know the rules, vigilance is the name of the game in our profession. It's my fault for letting my enthusiasm and sincerity get the better of me...

Anyway, a meeting like this has to have been written in the stars. Ask me anything you like — I won't skimp on the details. Still, make it snappy, you're never more than ten feet from a Silvermane Guard...
Is there a settlement nearby?
Settlement? What a literary turn of phrase. Why, there's only one place in this world where the living still reside — our beloved Belobog! The further away you get, the dicier things become.

The City of Preservation, the Towering Citadel, humanity's last bastion against the Eternal Freeze... It may sound a bit over the top, but those names are grounded in truth. The only place humans can eke out an existence is behind those impregnable walls.
Why were you hiding in the snow?
Me? You guys scared me to death... There I was looking for relics to sell, when all of a sudden you came stomping over. I thought the Silvermane Guards were paying me a visit.
Seriously though, try treading a little lighter next time, hmm? If you run into the Guards, they won't hide in a snowdrift... and you'll be in a cell before you know it.
I have no idea who these Silvermane Guards even are...

You...You really don't know? The Silvermane Guards are Belobog's soldiers, enforcers, and police. Let's just say they're not the most flexible of people... and they like paying visits to folks in our line of work.

Seems like you guys really are new to the business. *sigh* To be young and naive again... How about this. As a senior in the field, which I'm sure you don't mind me saying, I'll give you some free guidance.

There are ways of doing things in this profession, and you better get familiar with them. Moving in the shadows, finding the goods, pricing your stock, hiding from the Guards... there's an art to all of it.
No need, why don't you just take us to the city? We don't really know the way.
The city? Already? I haven't even started trading yet. Showing you the way is easy enough, missy, but it would cost—
...B—But it would be my pleasure! "Kindness" is Sampo Koski's middle name. Follow me, friends, and keep quiet. We don't want to be spotted by the Guards.
...And the prime suspect? The one with the blue hair?
Apologies, Captain! W—We lost him during the pursuit. We can't find his footprints...
*sigh* No matter, we have his accomplices. He'll be close by, plotting his next move.
We're not his accomplices.
Yeah, we'd never team up with someone like him!
You might be waiting longer than you think...
...As in, forever.
I'm not trying to talk our way out of this, but... we're not friends with that scoundrel. Did you see how fast he ditched us?
We rescued him from the snow out of the kindness of our hearts. We had no idea he might be using us to get past you! Are you really dumb enough to fall for his...
I'm a captain, not an adjudication panel. As a Belobog citizen, you have the right to defend yourself, but that can only take place under the scrutiny of the Architects, not now.
Take them away.
But we're not from Belobog!
Take a look at our clothes.
Silence! What kind of nonsense are you—
As you were. We must not be tempted into careless judgment. Look at their attire. Indeed, it is not in the Belobog style.
Exactly! A—And we even have photos!
Does our equipment bear any resemblance to yours?
As you were. We must not be tempted into careless judgment. Look at their relics. We've never excavated anything like them before, and I haven't seen anything similar in our museums.
Show him the photos, March.
Photos?
Ah! {NICKNAME}, you're a genius! Great idea!
You've probably never seen what your planet looks like, right? I took this one. Behold, Jarilo-VI...
March 7th shows Gepard a picture of the ice-covered planet...
...You mean to say that this... white ball... That's here? That's our home? How can that...

It is said that a long time ago, {RUBY_B#Interstellar Travelers}strange visitors from beyond the sky{RUBY_E#} would visit us here... but that after the Eternal Freeze, the blizzards made passage impossible... and Belobog would cease to witness such arrivals.
But these people are—
This decision is beyond us. If what they say is true, then only the supreme guardian may decide their fate.
Our job is to present them before her. Nothing more.
Outsiders, follow me. Belobog lies beyond this blizzard.
Welcome to Belobog — the City of Preservation.
This place still hasn't been corroded, yet Fragmentum monsters have already made it here.
I fear the Stellaron may be exerting a significant influence on this world.
These buildings have been buried in the snowfall.
Huh!? So these are rooftops? How long would snow have to fall to get this thick?
...A long, long time.
This is Voidranger armor. It's ancient.
Voidranger? Was this planet invaded by the Antimatter Legion?
I don't know.
*gasp* Did you see that? I think something's moving...
Mm... It's just an ordinary snowdrift. Are you sure you're not seeing things?
Of course not, my eyesight's perfect! Come on, let's take a closer look.
So why were you hiding from the Silvermane Guards?
Uhh, I was just storing a few relics away from prying eyes, nothing serious. If it weren't for the uncompromising nature of our civil service, there'd be no need for secrecy.
So whereabouts are you guys from, anyway? I don't mean to pry or anything, I just care about my friends! No pressure...
...Rule number seven: Never leave a footprint. I have my own special technique called "invisible snow-walking." Helps me throw off pursuers in no...time...
...Who are they?
Uh, you remember the Silvermane Guards I mentioned? That's them...
Help me, old friends! I don't wanna be caught!
It's the suspect and his accomplices! Arrest them!
It's now or never!
Over to you, dear friends!
Hey! Where do you think you're—
I, Gepard Landau, captain of the Silvermane Guards, order you to relinquish your futile resistance.
Grr, that Sampo cheated us all. Wait till I get my hands on him...
Suspect! Relinquish your resistance!
Ugh, so I'm a criminal, huh? Forget Sampo, wait until I get my hands on YOU!
{NICKNAME}, March, this Gepard... he's no pushover.
In the name of Preservation!
(If we don't keep up with this guy, we might get lost in the blizzard...)
Need any help, Dr. Natasha?
You came at a good time, {NICKNAME}, there is something you can help me with.
According to my patient records, there are a few that haven't come for their follow-up visits. It happens from time to time, but never as regularly as this. I'm a bit concerned...
Have you heard of the Complex Illness Mutual Aid Society?
Sounds like a charitable organization.
Sounds suspicious...
Mm, I agree.

Generally speaking, mutual aid societies like these allow patients to share their experiences and support each other. It's a way of countering all the negative emotional effects of being ill... But there might be more to this society than that.
I've got a few patients who've started refusing treatment since joining the society... It certainly makes you wonder.
The most suspicious part is that no matter how much I ask, no one's ever willing to tell me anything about it... and that's where you might be able to help.
Got it, you want me to go undercover.
...It sounds dangerous, but what I want you to do is actually very simple. Investigate this so-called "Mutual Aid Society" and find out what exactly they're up to.
Do I need to be ill before I can make inquiries?
...That won't be necessary, but it will help if you pretend to be a patient. Help me investigate this so-called "Mutual Aid Society" and find out exactly what they're up to.
What should I do?
Hmm... Pretend to be a patient. Help me investigate this so-called "Mutual Aid Society" and find out exactly what they're up to.
If I find out they're preventing me from doing my job... or if they're bringing harm to my patients... I won't just sit on the sidelines.
Can I entrust you with this task, {NICKNAME}?
No problem, leave it with me.
Have I ever refused you?
You're as considerate as always, {NICKNAME}.
This little clinic has huge numbers of patients to deal with every day... If I didn't have you here to help me out, I wouldn't be able to focus on giving them quality care.
Good luck, {NICKNAME}. I'll be sure to thank you properly when you're back.
You... I've seen you at the clinic. You run errands for Natasha, right?
Well, there goes my cover...
...Your cover? What are you talking about?
Uh... Who's Natasha?
...Don't play dumb. I might be sick but my eyes still work.
*sigh* Let me guess, Natasha wants you to persuade me to go back for a follow-up visit, right?
*sigh* ...What's the use? I'm terminal. Life'll be over before I know it.
Was that Natasha's diagnosis?
Of course not, I read it in a book.
Every book I read has descriptions that match my symptoms exactly... I can diagnose myself with a dozen incurable diseases before I get halfway through.
For people in my situation, a follow-up visit is just a waste of time and money... not to mention medicine.
Are you serious?
Soooo nothing to do with you joining the mutual aid society then?
Mutual aid what now? What are you talking about?
...What else is there to say. Natasha was seeing me free of charge. She said I could keep a tab running for as long as I liked, then pay it back when I had the opportunity... I guess I'm too proud.
Money's one thing, but life...
You think I need you to tell me? Don't try and persuade me, I've already thought this through...
Appearances are more important than life, I feel you.
...Are you making fun of me? Have at it, you won't change my mind.
*sigh* ...Dr. Vache never charged me anything either. Natasha's great, but Vache was always my number one...
Who's Dr. Vache?
Natasha's brother? They both used to practice medicine back in Rivet Town.
I heard he was a top student from the Overworld medical academy — Belobog's main hospital wanted him. I've no idea what convinced him to set up down here... a kind heart, maybe.
Free medical care? I don't believe it...
What do you mean? Dr. Vache was a people's doctor — he handed out free medicine. He even followed up with detailed questions on how we felt.
The Underworld is always short on medical resources — they say that Dr. Vache made all his own medicine himself.
Why don't you go to him anymore?
You think I don't want to? I heard that he... passed away.
Uh... I should keep my voice down. Don't go telling anyone else about this next bit...
I won't.
I heard that Natasha had something to do with Dr. Vache's death. They say she was jealous that her brother had stolen her patients, so she...
And you believe that?
Agh, it's just something people were saying... I don't think Dr. Natasha could do something like that.
It's not impossible...
...Hey, it's just a rumor. Don't take my word for it.
*sigh* Forget I said anything. Since Dr. Natasha sent you over specially, I'll do her a favor.
I'll go to the clinic for my follow-up a little later. Bye for now...
(Avoiding a follow-up visit due to money issues...)
(I should find another patient to talk to...)
...What was that? You'll have to be louder! My ears aren't what they used to be — everything's muffled.
I wanted to ask why you're not going for your follow-up visit.
Hah? Follow-up visit? Is that what you're asking about?
*sigh* Natasha's a wonderful girl. She always gives me a thorough checkup...
But at this age, it's rather a lot to bear. Even if they could cure me, I'm sure I wouldn't be around for long. I don't want to waste anyone's time...
There's no time wasted where health is concerned, right?
Not for youngsters like yourself. When you get to my time of life, good health is a bit of a luxury I'm afraid.
You should listen to Dr. Natasha.
That girl's always trying to get me to take my medicine on time. *sigh* I know her heart's in the right place...
My husband had the same illness as me, but he never touched the medicine. He wanted to make sure I had enough.
Then one day, he said he needed to take care of some things at the mine. He never came back...
He was forever saying he wanted to go before I did. Hehe... Selfish old fool...
I miss him. Now that he's gone, who cares how long I stick around?
I'm sure he's up there caring right now.
...Do you think so? Wouldn't he want me to hurry up and join him...?
Hmph... Kids today don't give up easily.
Dr. Natasha cares.
...You're not wrong, I suppose. That girl certainly spares me no effort, but I always feel like I'm a burden to her...
I care.
You don't give up easily, do you? Still... you're full of kind words.
Okay, you win. It's off for another follow-up visit with Dr. Natasha, I suppose...
Mm? Did you want to say something else? My ears are terrible...
Have you heard of the mutual aid society?
Virtual who?
Mutual aid society!
Alright, I heard you! Do you have to shout? ...No, I've never heard of any mutual aid society...
(Avoiding a follow-up visit due to her husband...)
(I should find another patient to talk to...)
Why haven't I gone for my follow-up visit... Are you a patient too, or did Dr. Natasha send you over?
What makes you say that?
Who else would care about people like me?
You're pretty sharp.
Hah, you should head on back then. Thank Dr. Natasha for her concern.
I don't need Dr. Natasha's help now. Tell her to save her worries and medicine for other people.
Did you have a dispute with her?
A dispute? No, no, she's the only kindhearted doctor in the Underworld.
I just don't really approve of her methods, that's all. Too idealistic, and no real efficacy...
I'm through seeing her too...
Huh? So you had a dispute with her?
...She's the only kindhearted doctor in the Underworld. I just don't really approve of her methods, that's all. Too idealistic, and no real efficacy...
She tries to save everyone, which means she can't save anyone... In the end, it's the patients who suffer, and she just tires herself out.
Miners like me don't have time for lengthy treatments... If I can't take something and get right back to work, I may as well lie down and wait for death to come knocking...
Did you know Dr. Vache? His wonder medicine is cheap and the results are immediate. You just need to be willing to... take a little risk.
"Risk"?
Dr. Vache's medicine is... different. Lots of people make a full recovery after taking it... but some get worse, and the unlucky ones check out early.
Even knowing the risk, most people fought tooth and nail to get a hold of the medicine. You know why?
They're willing to gamble with their life...
Hmph, you're smarter than you look.
I've no idea.
Hmph... you've clearly never been in really dire straits.
When life forces you to the edge, you'll throw yourself at any opportunity... even if it means risking it all.
For people like us, a slow and tortuous treatment is the same as a death sentence. If it's between that and a quick result, we'll take the latter.
Ahem, forget it. Why am I telling you all this? Dr. Vache is dead, anyway...
Where can I go to get this wonder medicine?
What if I told you I agreed with you?
Hah, what, now you're interested in the wonder medicine?
Listen up... the Complex Illness Mutual Aid Society is still selling that medicine... I can tell you where they trade, but there's a rule...
...You must not tell any of this to Dr. Natasha, you hear? If you break the rule, you'll face the consequences!
Here, take this, it's the address. A final warning — do not reveal this information to Natasha!
(I know where to find the wonder medicine. What should I do next...?)
(That patient didn't want me to tell Natasha about this... Should I listen to him?)
Let's tell Natasha first.
Let's investigate the wonder medicine address first.
Explain what you found out about the mutual aid society.
So the mutual aid society found my bro— ...Vache's research results... and now they're selling this so-called "wonder medicine" to patients...?
Any organization doing something like that is interested in more than just "mutual aid..."
The patients wanted me to keep it a secret from you.
I'm not surprised. They'll know that I'm completely against them using this "wonder medicine..."
The patient said he was willing to take the risk.
...As a doctor, I don't accept that — I'm responsible for their well-being. My attitude towards this "wonder medicine" won't change.
What Vache left behind is nothing more than reagents and experimental by-products... The word "medicine" doesn't apply here.
I warned the patients countless times, but it seems like they had their heads in the sand all along... No wonder they kept the mutual aid society a secret from me.
Thank you, {NICKNAME}. Those patients weren't exactly singing my praises — thank you for having faith in me.
If you're curious about Vache's wonder medicine, you should ask some of the patients in the clinic... see what they have to say about the effects.
Hey, where do you think you're going?
To buy medicine from the mutual aid society.
Medicine? Oh... you mean Dr. Vache's wonder medicine, right?
Just taking a walk...
In the Fragmentum? Hmph, gimme a break.
You're the same as everyone else that comes through here. If you want medicine, you don't need to go any further — you talk to me.
And we only take cash, this ain't a charity...
I heard the medicine here is pretty cheap.
The mutual aid society sets the price. It might be different from Dr. Vache and his handouts, but it's a darn sight cheaper than that clinic woman's medicine.
...Well, are you buying or not? Spit it out. I don't have time for chit-chat.
What if a patient doesn't have the money?
No money? Then you don't get any. You go home and wait for death.
...Say, what are you trying to pull here? If you can't afford it, then get outta my sight. I've got medicine to sell.
I'll take a course of treatment.
Hmph, cut the small talk next time... my time is valuable.
Must be difficult being this unpleasant.
Huh? What are you gonna do about it? Either buy something or clear out.
Shouldn't you think about those in need?
You sound like Vache. That isn't how the mutual aid society works.
Wait a minute, your clothes... Are you friends with that doctor woman? I've seen you at the clinic before — I know it!
Get lost — now! If you're a friend of that woman then you're not welcome here! Shop's closed today, no customers!
...W—Wait! What about our medicine? We've been waiting for ages...
Get lost! All of ya! Save your breath and come back some other time!
...Th—This is all your fault! How are we supposed to get our wonder medicine now!?
You should leave — if you stay here that guy might not ever sell to us again...
(That medicine seller sure shut up shop in a hurry...)
(I should head back and report to Natasha.)
Explain what you found out about the mutual aid society.

Any organization doing something like that is interested in more than just "mutual aid..."

...As a doctor, I don't accept that — I'm responsible for their well-being. My attitude towards this "wonder medicine" won't change.
