I'm guessing the patients you met weren't exactly singing my praises, which is why you tracked the dealer down and made inquiries first.
I don't blame you, {NICKNAME}. After everything you heard, I'm grateful you came back to find me. Your trust is important to me.
If you're curious about Vache's wonder medicine, you should ask some of the patients in the clinic... see what they have to say about the effects.
The medicine Vache left behind? That stuff... Can you even call it medicine?
I know Dr. Natasha's here, but I have to tell it like it is... Vache had zero medical ethics — he didn't deserve the title "doctor."
He may have had the capability, but he didn't use it to help anyone... Whenever I went to see him, he never even asked about my illness! He just prescribed me his so-called "wonder medicine..."
If it were you, would you have taken that medicine?
Some people say that Dr. Vache was a saint who came from the Overworld to help those in need... I don't buy it.

"People's doctor..." That's just what people who've bought into the myth like to say. Vache used to distribute free medicine all the time, but, uh... he couldn't have cared less about the people taking the medicine...
The hard truth is that we were just his test subjects. It didn't matter if the medicine worked or not. What mattered was having a constant stream of willing lab rats...
...Of course, I can't control what anyone else thinks. That's just how I see it.
...I still haven't worked out how to convey it to you, the issues surrounding Vache. My relationship with him... the things he's done in the Underworld... it's a long story.
I'm guessing you've heard a lot of different opinions on Vache. What do you make of him, {NICKNAME}?
I think he was a doctor with zero medical ethics.
It's tough for me to say.
I think he's insane.
I see... I can understand that.
{NICKNAME}, I want you to go and visit another patient — a victim of the wonder medicine... I want you to see the real consequences of abusing that medicine.
Once you've understood her situation, come back and tell me what you think. After that... I want to ask for your help again.
That's the patient, {NICKNAME}.
Watch what you say to her, she's not in the most stable mental state... I've taken care of her for a long time, but still haven't been able to get her back to her old self.
Try talking with her, {NICKNAME}. And try to be as kind as possible... you don't want to scare her.
...Who are you...?
I'm a friend of Dr. Natasha.
I'm a... miracle doctor from beyond the sky.
...Who? And... who am I?
You haven't introduced yourself yet.
You're one of Dr. Natasha's patients, don't you remember?
...Where's my husband... and where's my child...?
...Wh—Where are they? You... you know where they are, right?
I'm afraid not. Are you okay?
Try and stay calm...
...You don't know... they don't know... nobody knows...
Where... Wh—Where did they go...
That poor, poor lady... Both her husband and child became ill and passed away.
They must have been seriously ill...
*sigh* ...Not terribly serious. But they needed to get treatment every now and then, which did impact their livelihood.
And that made her become like this?
Yes... Before her family passed away, she was a carefree young woman.
Her husband and child caught a mysterious illness. The symptoms weren't grave, but their livelihood was certainly impacted.

In order to try and rid themselves of the ailment once and for all, they bought some kind of "wonder medicine..." Who would've thought their condition would deteriorate so rapidly after they began using it.
The two began to suffer terribly, such that death became a blessing... It wasn't long before they departed this world, one after the other.
From that moment on, oh she became as you see her now. If Dr. Natasha hadn't taken her under her wing... *sigh* Well it doesn't bear thinking about.
It just sounds like poison...
And yet what more could've been done? They were warned about the medicine. They were told about the risks... They chose to roll the dice.
They were unlucky...
Just unlucky? As far as I'm concerned, those medicine dealers are making money for murder in broad daylight... Who would sell such a thing to the sick?
*sigh* Talking about it tires me out. At least my husband and I are able to help her where we can. I just hope that one day she can lead a normal life again...
Come over here, child. It's best to leave that poor lady in peace. Let me explain...
What's wrong with her? Isn't it obvious? Her family were the victims of improper medical treatment, then she had a nervous breakdown...
*sigh* Oh sister, sometimes there just isn't a cure...
That Dr. Vache wasn't human... he was a devil in a doctor's coat!
I told her so many times not to believe in that medicine, but she...
...I heard that Vache died?
Yeah... But don't think for a second he was any better than those medicine dealers at the mutual aid society. He was worse than they could ever aspire to be!
At least the mutual aid society doesn't hide the risk from the buyers. Vache gave that poison away to everyone for free... even the elderly and the children...
Argh, I hate them! I hate them all! How could they do this to my sister...
Did you speak to her, {NICKNAME}?
By the look on your face... I'm assuming you've come to understand the wonder medicine all too well.
The people selling that stuff are devils.
Those medicine dealers prey on our weaknesses...
Be it Vache or the mutual aid society — forces like that can take full advantage of the... the typical Underworld state of mind.
Let me tell you a story, {NICKNAME}.
There was once a brilliant Overworld doctor with unmatched pharmaceutical skill.
The doctor was set on developing a medicine that would steel the human body against the cold. He named his research project "Blizzard Immunity."

But his research met with obstruction time and time again, the biggest factor being a lack of test subjects. Tampering with the human immune system carries huge risk, and nobody in the Overworld was willing to submit themselves to such experiments.
As such, the doctor got in touch with his sister in the Underworld... claiming that he wanted to support the medical effort below ground.
And then...
...Naturally, his sister was overjoyed. After all, as far as medicine was concerned, her brother had always been the standard she'd strived to attain.
She brought her brother underground and entrusted him with her clinic and laboratory...
...I think you know what comes next.
I'm sorry that I doubted you before...
It's hard to believe he was your brother...
Issuing free medicine to the needy was just Vache's way of conducting experiments on his test subjects.
On some level, his reagents were able to alleviate the patients' suffering... but nothing more. They would forget their pain for a while, and neglect their regular treatment plans...
The result... patients with mild illness would attribute their recovery to the so-called wonder medicine, while patients with serious illness would quickly deteriorate... and sometimes die.
I cannot accept that their fate was simply the result of misfortune or risk, {NICKNAME}. No true doctor would accept that.
That's why I want you to help me recover all the wonder medicine. Are you willing to take on this assignment?
Somebody has to do the right thing.
Not my preferred course of action, but...
...But it's impossible to sit on the sidelines, right?
Thank you, {NICKNAME}.
This will be hard for the people that have come to rely on the wonder medicine... but it's up to us to remove this false hope.
You mustn't hesitate — recover every last reagent that Vache left behind. I'll take responsibility for the consequences — don't worry about that.
Go, {NICKNAME}. I'll be waiting for the good news.
Stop right there! No one's allowed up ahead!
Hand over the wonder medicine.
Oh-ho! Playing the hero, are we? Is this a stick-up?
You're that clinic woman's lackey, aren't you. Did you think the mutual aid society didn't have its own intel?
I'm here to buy.
Who are you trying to kid? You're that clinic woman's lackey. Did you think the mutual aid society didn't have its own intel?
I'm just taking a walk...
In the Fragmentum? Gimme a break!
You're that clinic woman's lackey, aren't you. Did you think the mutual aid society didn't have its own intel?
She's after our medicine and sent you here to smash the place, right?
Men, look lively and send this idiot packing already!
The old box has some medicine labeled with experiment numbers. This must be the wonder medicine the mutual aid society was talking about.
You suddenly hear footsteps behind you...
...Well, look who we have here. Your reputation precedes you, outsider... I didn't take you for a bandit and a thief!
Who are you?
I'm just passing through.
Oh, just passing through... And our guards decided to just beat themselves into submission, I suppose?
You listen here — I'm the president of the Complex Illness Mutual Aid Society. The medicine we hold here is lifeblood for many of our members. Are you sure you want to deprive them of that?
Those poor patients... Along comes a life-saving wonder medicine, only to be snatched away by a shameless bandit like you...
The Underworld is full of sickness... What would happen if we left it all to that clinic to treat?
My mutual aid society has relieved that doctor of patients at the end of the road. Shouldn't she be thanking me?
Natasha would never give up on a patient...
...And she'd never work with an impostor like you!
Hmm. Seems like you are quite bent on dismantling our operations, aren't you?
Fine, seeing as you came all this way, it'd be rude not to give you the opportunity!
Men, seize the medicine thief!
Blast it... What did we ever do to you? Why are you taking away our money-maker!?
"...Money-maker"?
So you admit it, then? You're not in this to save lives. You're in it to get rich.
Wh—What are you doing here? Ugh, as if we didn't have enough trouble already...
...Selling fake medicine with false kindness. You should have expected trouble to find you sooner or later.
I have a responsibility to protect the well-being of my patients... or to put it another way: I must eradicate any and all threats to them.
You... You can't save everyone! The Underworld is teeming with sickness... how could you possibly pull it off!
You're right, I can't save everyone alone... but if I must, I would sacrifice food and sleep to treat them.
The debt that Vache owes to the Underworld rests with me. All I can do is help everyone to the best of my ability... to the very end.
Ugh... So stubborn... In that sense, you're no different from your crazy brother.
...I'll take that as a compliment.
Thank you, {NICKNAME}. Your actions today have saved many Underworld families.
I'll find a way to dispose of Vache's leftover reagents. Next time the "Mutual Aid Society" wants to whip up a quack cure? They'll be out of luck.
Let's go back to town. I still owe those patients an explanation...
(It looks like the patients have surrounded Natasha? Let's hear what they're saying...)
...What are you saying, doctor? The wonder medicine is out of supply?
Correct. That medicine is a wolf in sheep's clothing — Wildfire has cut off the supply chain.
Your ailments need rational, scientific treatment. Relying on pseudo-medicines will only worsen your condition...
Hmph, rational and scientific, huh...? The way I see it, you're just jealous you lost your patients.
H—How dare you speak to Dr. Natasha like that! Where are your manners...
...Ma'am, please think for a moment. How can you still be siding with her? That wonder medicine was working fine for us, and now it's gone because she wants it to be? How can she—
I understand your anger, but as your doctor, I ask you to trust my judgment.
I will find a way to access more medical resources and help you through your struggles. If I must, I'll get help from the surface...
The surface... Hmph, I almost forgot that you were an Overworld big shot.
Have some respect for Dr. Natasha...
Tsk, if it's respect she wants, she better find a replacement for the wonder medicine, fast! If not, I'll tell everyone about how she set up Dr. Vache.
I'm out of here!
Oh... {NICKNAME}, you're here. I apologize, that must have made for uncomfortable viewing.
Are you okay?
Mm... I'm okay. If I were in his shoes, I may well have had the same reaction. Now I need to focus on treating the patients, and dispelling their doubts.
I'd like to straighten out that loudmouth myself!
Don't let your emotions get the better of you. If I were in his shoes, I might well have had the same reaction. Now I need to focus on treating the patients, and dispelling their doubts.
...Let's leave it for now. I'll feel a lot better once I've gotten rid of this mess that Vache left us.
...Now's as good a time as any to tell you Vache's whole story.
If there's anything you want to know, don't hesitate to ask.
Was he your biological brother?
No... but I used to think we were so close that we may as well have been...
I actually grew up in the orphanage. It wasn't until I was adopted by an Overworld family that life changed for me.
My adoptive mother always saw me as her own flesh and blood, and Vache loved me like a sister... that is, while we were still young.

My adoptive parents belonged to a prominent medical family — as kids, we were exposed to all kinds of medical texts. When we were older, both of us got straight into Belobog's medical school. We were on a path into the medical profession.
What kind of person was Vache?
He was gentle and introverted. But when it came to work he could be absurdly obsessive... like a completely different person.
Whenever I made a mistake in an experiment, he'd bite my head off... and then a while later, he'd apologize and comfort me. He was conflicted in that way.
So you knew this medicine was his work?
I didn't know he had leftover reagents in Rivet Town. I was shocked when you told me.
If you fail to make a clean break with the past, the past creeps up on you...
Did he...really pass away?
*sigh* That's a long story... Ever since he was little, Vache had always wanted to develop a medicine called "Blizzard Immunity."

He saw the human body's vulnerability to cold as a disease, and wanted to cure it so that humanity could survive the Eternal Freeze. If he succeeded, people would be able to leave Belobog and rebuild their homes in the Snow Plains.
Do you share his vision?
To be honest, I never understood how he'd achieve that "Blizzard Immunity." But I do admire that vision and perseverance... I always chose to believe him, ever since I was a kid.
(Brief silence)
I do admire his vision and perseverance, even though "Blizzard Immunity" always seemed unachievable to me.

I knew his research in the Overworld wasn't going well. I used to write to him and ask him to come down and stay with the kids in the orphanage for a while. I thought it might help take his mind off his research.
But I was too young to know what long-term frustration could do to a person. It changed him in a terrible way...
Changed him...?

During his stay in the Underworld, he met patients affected by Fragmentum corrosion with mild symptoms. Compared with non-patients, their bodies reacted differently to hot and cold. And that fascinated Vache.
He began to simulate mild Fragmentum corrosion, thinking that it could lead to breakthroughs in developing Blizzard Immunity.

Those reagents of his aren't cure-alls for critical illness — that doesn't exist. Vache made the reagents to mitigate the suffering of his patients in the short term — a convenient way for him to observe changes in his test subjects.

But behind my back, he had been doling out the reagents to residents who were kept in the dark. When it finally struck me that something was wrong, his terrible research had already turned him into... into a madman.
He'd lost his last shred of humanity...
Indeed... and it all happened under my nose. How ridiculous — my judgment was clouded by trust in a loved one...
Did nothing seem strange to you all that time?
I trusted Vache with all my heart. Funny, isn't it? And pathetic.
When his experiments were exposed, I spent a long time with Oleg discussing how to handle the aftermath.
This was shortly before the Underworld was sealed off — there were hardly any Silvermane Guards remaining. We spent ages trying to find a way to handle Vache.
In the end, Oleg suggested that we banish him and permanently deny him access to the Underworld.

Had his victims found out the truth, Vache would've been torn to pieces by furious Underworlders. I was young and weak at the time — Oleg must have worried about how I'd react to such a scenario, or he wouldn't have suggested banishment.
Banishment isn't a particularly harsh punishment...
*sigh* Looking back, it wasn't. He deserved much worse...
You two did the right thing.
...I hope so. The day I learned the truth was the day I no longer recognized my brother.
Oleg and I took Vache to the Overworld. He made his final request to us: To take him outside the city to the Snow Plains he'd always wanted to conquer.
His figure gradually disappeared into the snow curtain... I've been telling myself that Vache is dead ever since.
Forgive me, {NICKNAME}, I'm not good at telling stories. Vache was a terrible brother and a worse doctor... That's all you need to know.
Let's call it a day. Thank you for cleaning up the mess my brother left behind. Here — for your trouble.
The Legion is gone, and the Curios are back. Various departments are returning to their research, and the newly imported goods from the cosmos are beginning to circulate.
Everything is going smoothly with Project Revival. So what exactly does this letter mean?
I heard you are looking for me?
{NICKNAME}, you're back. Just in time!
Thanks to your help and everybody's hard work, the space station is pretty much back on its feet.
As a conclusion to Project Revival, I wanted to summon you to witness the fruits of our labor.
But just two days ago, I received a strange letter. Now that you're here, perhaps you can help me figure out what it is about.
I often hear the researchers praise you for your resourcefulness and good judgment. What do you think? Any clue what this message is about?
It seems like something from the Department of Implement Arts.
Yes, only the researcher called Wen in the Department of Implement Arts would speak like that.

However, it was a strange story how I got hold of this letter at the beginning. It was sandwiched in a tome called A Guide to Astral Realm Species on the Conference Room table. Normally, no one looks at it except me.
Obviously, someone wanted to hand me this letter in private, so I didn't dare to ask the staff in the Department of Implement Arts.
Who is this Cryptologist From Locus Silentii?
As far as I know, there is no one with this title in the space station. It must be an alias.
But the identity of the writer is not what I am most concerned about.
Spirit sounds particularly familiar.
Spirit... Spirit... Can it be... The Xenohydro? Well done, {NICKNAME}! You just found the "key" to the text right away. Now everything makes sense!
It seems this is no ordinary letter, it's from an informant. Their intention is to report on the Xenohydro.
The Xenohydro has disappeared from the space station since it escaped from Mr. Wen Mingde's hands.
This letter seems to support the rumor that the Xenohydro was not caught because it has an accomplice.

Look at this sentence. "An inquiry into spirit traces, a glance into the site of storage" is obviously leading us to investigate the Xenohydro's range of activities, and "to be an accomplice" implies the existence of an accomplice.

As for the other six sentences, in my opinion, some depict the portrait of the accomplice and some describe the real hiding place of the Xenohydro. Unfortunately, I have no idea how to interpret the rest of the message.
Now that we are done with other work, this letter falls into our hands at just the right moment. It's high time we put the Xenohydro issue back on the table. {NICKNAME}, what do you think?
I am with you all the way!
I have a lot going on lately...
Please, {NICKNAME}. I hope you won't refuse. After all—

Considering there may be a traitor among us, if I hand this case to our staff, we might alert the culprit. And {NICKNAME}, you're not a staff member, and you've also met the Xenohydro before. You really are the ideal candidate to handle this case.

And if there is an accomplice involved, this matter is no longer a simple case of Curio retrieval. It must be handled with caution. Therefore, I would like to ask you to go to the Storage Zone mentioned in the letter and verify the facts.
If we can catch either the Xenohydro or the accomplice, we'll be able to interrogate them. Then I can judge whether the accomplice's motive is malicious or not.
At this critical juncture, it is up to us to finally finish Project Revival.
I've always been a rather magnanimous person. In fact, here is a chance for you to regain my favor... As long as you are willing to apologize for your behavior!
I didn't do those things...
You want to deny the truth!? Lamina, Lamina, you're getting more and more dishonest! Let me help you remember—
The mustard in my lunch box, the big hole on the back of my uniform, and this boring letter in reply to the female researcher. Aren't they your doing?
It's true I'm the only person who handled those things, but...

And when I was reporting to Miss Asta, you suddenly shouted, "Mr. Capote, it's too late. The Wubbaboos are still waiting for you to play with them!" You made her think I was colluding with Curios and not doing my job.
But I was just stating a fact...
We should keep it only between you, and me! How many times have I told you that? You were just going against me on purpose!
Forget it. I don't think you are going to repent at all. One day, when you're sick of this place and your future is gloomy, you will come crawling back to seek help from me.
Just keep praying that by then, I haven't replaced you with a Renona, an Elena, or a Barbara... or someone else, hmph!
When can I become braver?
Oh, it's {NICKNAME}, the hero of the space station. I've heard so much about you. I didn't expect to have the opportunity to see you up close.
What are you doing here?
I... I was Mr. Capote's secretary.
But recently, I made a few mistakes when I was running errands for him. So he sent me here to work on the Curio sorting assembly line.
I'm so sorry, you must think I am a joke...
You did all those things?
You heard it all... Although, I don't remember doing the things Mr. Capote accused me of.
I also suspected someone else, but everything showed that I was the only one who touched Mr. Capote's things.
Maybe "Lamina's law" is really true. In the Department of Ecology, they have a saying, anything that Lamina "can" screw up, Lamina will "screw up."
Don't rush to judgment yet.
{NICKNAME}, do you think... there's another explanation for this? Surely not...
That's an interesting law!
Come on, how would you feel if it was called the "{NICKNAME}'s law."
I have a letter for you to read.
Sure, but knowing me, I probably won't be much help...

Well, if I understand correctly, where it says, "An inquiry into spirit traces," it seems to be referring to the Xenohydro, a kind of Curio from our department. And "to be an accomplice" seems to be some kind of accusation.
{NICKNAME}, why are you asking me this? Are you investigating the escape of the Xenohydro?
It's in the storage zone.
Oh!? Really... I've been hanging around here lately, but I haven't noticed anything unusual.
Maybe it's impersonating you?
Huh!? Did it do those things that Mr. Capote is accusing me of? But why...
As for the rest of the letter, please forgive my ignorance, but I really don't understand it.
But now we know it's in the Storage Zone, and this area is only so large. Maybe we can take the initiative and make a list of the possible suspects.
I'm quite familiar with this place. There are one or two places I know that are inaccessible where the Xenohydro may be hiding. I can take you to have a look.
Actions are better than words. If you don't mind, {NICKNAME}, follow me.
Ahem, ehem, this room smells humid... It seems the Xenohydro really was here.
{NICKNAME}, come quickly. This place is secluded and it's a good vantage point. You can watch the whole room from here.
Well... Are you sure we want to ambush it here? We can try making a trap, it's one of our standard procedures in the Department of Ecology.
How do you make a trap?
Ambush it in person.
This may not be wise... According to the A Guide to Species in the Astral Realm, the Xenohydro is very cautious and stealthy. If we simply wait for it, it's probably just a waste of time.
{NICKNAME}, why don't I show you how to make a trap?
Tightly connect the two disposable kinetic arms. Once the prey steps within range of the power arm, all that awaits them is doom.
To make a disposable kinetic arm, we need to find many intricate parts, Strange Matter of Destruction and Phase Flame...
I am glad you have such a good memory.
No, astral ecology is a rigorous and beautiful discipline of knowledge. I am simply conveying its charm truthfully.
But you reminded me that it'll be difficult to gather all the materials quickly.
Sounds like fancy material.
It's okay. In the past, we could take as much as we wanted from the Department of Implement Arts. But now we are short of materials, it'll be hard to collect everything we need soon.
By that time the Xenohydro will have died of old age.
Well, it won't take quite that long. The Xenohydro has a pretty long lifespan... But we probably shouldn't put ourselves in such a passive situation.
Anyway, we'd better ambush it ourselves.
We may have to wait for a while. Why don't we have a chat to kill time, {NICKNAME}.
Why do you work for Capote?

Fersman is an old customer of mine. He's pretty nice to me, though we are not so close. As to what he did about that Geomarrow vein, it was kinda unethical.
We're all neighbors. We've known each other for a long time. But he sold out to the other side and left his own people out to dry... I really can't agree with that!
Did you see the detector?
Look, the cook is definitely the thief, I'm sure about that! I value my reputation more than anything, so you can trust me.
Why are you so sure about that?
In my line of work, I've learned to read people. And something's definitely fishy with that cook. I could tell from the start. If you don't believe me, just ask anyone.
Feels like you're trying to trick me.
What do I have to gain from lying to you? Wildfire coming for me in the night?
Trust me, something's definitely fishy with that cook. I could tell from the start. If you don't believe me, just ask anyone.
That cook is a crook. He's definitely the one who stole Fersman's device.
Huh, Hook? What's the matter?
Did you steal daddy's detector?
Wha— Oh if I'd known I would become a suspect, I wouldn't have gone out at that time... How foolish of me.
Relax. We're just checking off all the boxes.
Feeling guilty or something? You seem a bit off.
O—Of course not! I didn't do anything wrong...
We just need you to answer a few questions!
Okay... ask away. It would be good to clear myself of suspicion.
What were you doing when the crime occurred?
Nothing special. I just went out to get some fresh air.
Oh dear, oh dear... I know that's a lame alibi! But I swear it's the truth.
What do you think of Mr. Fersman?
Mr. Fersman? He's a good person. Though... oh, er, uh, never mind.
Oh no, oh no... I must sound very suspicious. But I really didn't do anything. You have to believe me...
Did you see the detector?
Detector? No, I haven't seen anything, and I don't know anything...
Is that all the questions you have? Have I proven my innocence?
Just stay calm and wait for the news.
I've figured it out. Be careful.
Oh dear... All this waiting around is enough to make me even more anxious...
I didn't steal it. Really, it wasn't me...
Argh... Hook's head is spinning! Do you remember everything they said?
Don't worry, I've written it down for you. Remember, among these four people, only the <color=#dbc291ff>real thief will lie</color>.
*sigh* The cook said the helper did it, the tailor said it wasn't her, the merchant said it was the cook, and the helper said it wasn't him. So, do you know who the culprit is?
Right, we have other methods besides deductive reasoning to find out who the true thief is. Let's just examine what they've said first to decide.
<color=#dbc291ff>The cook.</color>
<color=#dbc291ff>The tailor.</color>
<color=#dbc291ff>The merchant.</color>
<color=#dbc291ff>The helper.</color>
Boss Hook, what do you think?
Hmm... I don't know why, but I'll trust your judgment!
Come on, let's go accuse the culprit!
I think the <color=#dbc291ff>cook</color> and <color=#dbc291ff>merchant</color> are the most suspicious. My gut tells me that one of them is the culprit.
Don't worry. Even if you choose the wrong one, Pitch-Dark Hook the Great has other ways to uncover the true culprit.
Huh!? Where's the cook? Where did he go?
Beats me! I saw him running out in quite a panic.
Argh! That guy has to be guilty! Where is he running off to...
Probably trying to sell off the spoils.
So he's fleeing from justice, huh?
Oh yeah! I saw Mr. Sampo on the way to the mine when I came here... Could he be involved in this?
It definitely has something to do with him!
He's just trouble on legs.
Follow Hook, Mr. Sampo should be that way!
Surely Sampo is innocent!
...Heh, that would be a naive thing to believe.
Hook figured it out, you're the one who stole daddy's detector!
Wrong.
Wrong? Why? Explain yourself!
Brains.
Use your brains.
She's pretty stubborn about denying it... Should we think it over again?
Suppose the tailor is lying...
If she's lying, then that makes her the thief! But then, what the cook and merchant said would contradict each other...
{NICKNAME}, what actually happened here!?
...The culprit might be somebody else.
What! Can I even count on you?
Forget it, let's keep looking for the culprit!
I had it wrong...
What! Can I even count on you?
Forget it, let's keep looking for the culprit!
Hook figured it out, you're the one who stole daddy's detector!
You gotta be kidding me... You thought about it for that long, and came up with this conclusion?
Ah? You mean... we got it wrong?
I gave you the answer, and you still couldn't crack the case, detective!? Why don't you just go home!
You don't have to be so mean.
I already told you, it was the cook! Even if you asked me a hundred times, my answer would still be the cook!
You're just trying to trick us.
Huh!? Is it that hard for you to admit you were wrong? Have you ever heard of something called "logic"?
Just you wait. I'll find evidence, and then you'll be begging me for mercy!
Fine, go ahead and look!
Is it really not you?
Of course it's not me!
Hey, you're not questioning yourself, are you? Let's look for evidence and let him beg me for mercy!
Pff, right, I'd beg you for mercy. Go ahead, you'll understand once you find the truth.
I was wrong, my apologies.
I wouldn't lie to you, it was the cook. The cook did it, the cook!
Hmm... Let's go look around and see if there are any more clues.
Hook figured it out, you're the one who stole daddy's detector!
Wha— What? You have the wrong person, I didn't steal anything! Waaaah... I knew you'd suspect me. I shouldn't have returned to the shelter at that time. If only I hadn't returned to the shelter...
If you want to cry, go cry to Wildfire.
I really didn't do it, I don't know anything!
You... you just think I'm a pushover. That's why you're treating me like this! Wah...
What did you take from the tent?
T—Tent? I've never even been close to Mr. Fersman's tent...
This isn't personal, it's just deductive reasoning.
W— Well... you deduced wrong! What kind of reasoning are you even using!?
I beg you, I never even stole pocket money from my parents as a kid. Don't wrong an innocent person...
Hmm... Maybe he really isn't the thief. Hook doesn't think he's lying...
Are you questioning my reasoning?
My deduction might be a little flawed...
Just think about it! Swetta said that only the real thief would lie to us.
If the thief really is the helper, then what he and the merchant said would both be wrong!
My mistake...
Why haven't I noticed you being this smart before?
Hmph! Adults are all so unreliable! Let's go look for more clues.
Let's go look around where daddy kept the detector. Maybe we can find some clues there.
This is the tent that Fersman temporarily borrowed in the shelter. It looks like it has been rummaged and a <color=#dbc291ff>packaging label</color> has fallen on the ground.
This is the label from a supply box... I know where those boxes are!
That way, let's go take a look!
The pickaxe used by Fersman. He's supposed to be retired, but to make a living, Fersaman would still work in the mines with the vagrants.
The supply crate from the shelter, transported here after a long journey. Barely recognizable, some text is printed on the box: Rivet Town.
An empty supply crate from the shelter. Judging by its label, it was used to store emergency tents.
A supply crate from the shelter. It's wet, as if it has been salvaged from the underground river. Judging by its label, it was used to store emergency food.
Mr. Sampo's always at the clinic hanging around Miss Natasha. Hook thought he was really sick or something!
If he's working with the thief... then he's also a bad guy!
My friend, are you serious? This device is quite rare. Are you really willing to sell it to me at such a low price?
I mean, I love a sweet deal as much as anyone, but I still have common sense — there has to be a catch, right?
No, no, why are you making this so complicated? Do you want it or not? Just tell me!
You two, stop right there! Pitch-Dark Hook the Great has arrived!
Sampo, what are you doing here?
Just doing a little business. What's all the fuss?
That guy is a thief, he's trying to sell something he stole!
Tsk boy, I knew it was too good to be true!
That guy is a thief, he's trying to sell something he stole!
Tsk boy, I knew it was too good to be true!
I gotta make this clear: I have nothing to do with this fella! You have to trust me— Miss Hook, please don't point that thing at me, it's scary!
Hey! How can you sell me out like that! We had a deal...
You! You stole daddy's treasure! Diggertron will not spare you...!
This... this is all that old Fersman's fault! Just because he has this device I'm holding, he can make a fortune... It's not fair!
Umm, well... It seems you guys have some issues to sort out. So... maybe I should leave.
That's no reason for you to steal it.
What kind of a reason are you looking for? With the Underworld in such a sad state, how are we supposed to survive if we don't resort to robbing and stealing?
Fersman has his reasons...
The heck if I care! With the Underworld in such a sad state, how are we supposed to survive if we don't resort to robbing and stealing?
Hmph, anyway, I got the device now! Come take it... if you have the guts!
Guess you want to do this the hard way.
Okay, we'll take it then!
Diggertron... get ready!
...I'm not afraid of you!
Quiet! I'm going to give you a good butt-kicking!
Wait a second! Let's all just calm down! Is there something wrong with the source of this stuff? I mean, I've got nothing to do with it...
You got some guts taunting us yourself...
Hah, you sure talked tough for someone who can't fight! Come on, hand the detector over to Hook!
No... No! Daddy's treasure... It's broken!
Life is full of disappointments, sorry kid...
But... But...
Can it be repaired?
Hey, now this is Sampo's time to shine!
You're still here?
Of course! I wouldn't want to miss out on seeing you and Miss Hook's acts of heroism, would I?

Listen here, there's a fellow in Boulder Town they call Balaway the Miner's Lamp. He's an appraiser. Although he claims that he doesn't do appraisals anymore for ancient relics, he actually still does a bit behind the scenes for ones that are of especially high value.
I think this device of yours is probably worth a lot. It might be a good idea to try your luck with Balaway.

Here's a trick — first, pretend that you want to sell it for a low price, then wait for him to excitedly fix the device for you. After it's fixed, tell him you've changed your mind and you want to keep it for yourself.
This business tactic is what I call a "bait and switch." Pretty clever, huh?
Balaway the Miner's Lamp... Got it! Thanks, Mr. Sampo.
{NICKNAME}, let's go into town to find him!
Have a safe trip!
I was wondering if you could have a look at this detector.
I'm already retired from appraising ancient relics. So unless this detector is some kind of precious treasure...
Look at this! The detector's probe broke off, can you fix it?
Oh ho ho, this certainly is a rare relic! Let me take a closer look...
Yes, look extra close! You have to help Hook fix it!
This device... I've been in the business for a long time, but never have I seen an ancient relic like this one before.
I think this is probably beyond repair. But still, it is a rare treasure. Even broken, I'd be willing to pay a high price for it. What do you say?
Can we trust your appraisal?
Can you tell me more about it? I intend to sell it.
The detector's probe is gone, it's like searching for something without eyes or ears. Now it's nothing more than a pile of junk with no practical value.
I'm willing to offer a generous price for this thing. So, do you want to sell it or not?
Boss, I think we should go.
Maybe we should let Fersman decide what to do with it.
Alright then, let's go find daddy...
The detector's probe is gone, it's like searching for something without eyes or ears. Who's going to want a pile of junk?
I don't believe any other stores will buy it off you. Come on, I'll give you a nice deal.
We aren't going to sell it to you, you crooked profiteer!
Where have you been, Hook? I was just about to go looking for you. Come on, let's go home, I'll cook some salt-baked rock crabs for you.
What's wrong with this kid?
She's been like this ever since just now...
Why, what happened?
We found the vein detector.
Vein detector? The one I lost?
{NICKNAME} and Hook helped daddy catch the thief that stole it!
But... daddy's detector... is broken. It's all my fault... If only I could've found it sooner...
So it was stolen... You're not hurt are you, Hook?
I'm fine! Daddy, can you see if your detector still works?
Hmm... the Geomarrow Probe is damaged. I'm afraid this thing won't work anymore.
I'm sorry, daddy. I didn't help one bit...
What are you apologizing for? Thank you so much for looking out for me, Hook.
But, daddy's treasure... Waaaah...
Don't cry, Hook! Daddy's true treasure has been here all along. It was never lost or broken.
...Huh?
It is an adorable treasure indeed.
Huh, even you know what it is?
This treasure can even cry, you know?
It can... cry?
The detector helped me find lots of Geomarrow veins, and it saved the mining team a lot of money. In that respect, it was a very good thing.
But at the end of the day, the detector is just a tool. A true treasure must have irreplaceable importance to someone.
Hook... doesn't really understand.
Hahaha, that's okay. I'm saying some things that might seem strange, but you will understand some day.
So, the treasure daddy is talking about...
Is still happily running and jumping around.
Daddy...
{NICKNAME}, you're not allowed to see Hook cry! Go away!
Oh, it's {NICKNAME}. You are finally here! Come on, do me a favor. We are such good friends. You won't just watch me suffer, right?
We are not that close...
Oh, that's a bit harsh! We've been through ups and downs together, and now you just pretend you don't know me. How can you be so cruel?
You only come to me when you need help. You think I'm a robot?
Come on! Am I like that to you? Businessmen like us rely on nothing but trust. Why would I treat you like a robot? No! Of course I wouldn't!
Just do me a favor — I started a mining tool rental business in the mines, but I'm missing a few key tools. I want you to help me find them. How simple is that? A piece of cake, right?

The investment cost of this mining tool rental is still very high, and it's not easy to find a supplier. But I'm not worried about losing money. What matters is that some people really rely on this business to earn money to support their families.
What happened here?
Do you really care whether other people can support their families?
What do you mean by that? I've always had a big heart — think about how helpful I've been to you in the past. You can't deny it, can you?
Well, to put it simply, there were some minor accidents in the mining area earlier. You know what it's like — it was chaos. All the mining tools I bought at a high price were lost, and I was furious!

Coincidentally, not long ago, a customer ordered a set of equipment from me... Well... I'd like to go look for it myself, but the situation in the mining area is complicated. I hear there are Fragmentum monsters in some places...

Gosh, ordinary people like us can't get close at all. I want to ask you for a favor because you have such extraordinary skills and great connections. You are much better than me at this sort of thing!

Let me see, I lost three mining tools... It's a little hard to find them, but if you can help me find those three pieces of equipment, I'll give you a secret treasure map — how about that? A very attractive deal for you, wouldn't you say?
Three is too many. Can we make it one?
Come on! You don't know how much trouble one has to go through just to get a set of legit mining tools here underground. Heck! I've already invested so much money in this...
Treasure map? That sounds like a fraud...
This treasure map is absolutely real! I always do business with the utmost integrity. Don't be fooled by those scoundrels who are just jealous of me simply because I make good money!

The mining team has a rule that all miners must have all three pieces of equipment before they can go down the mine — I can't rent them out if I don't have all three of them. {M#My good man}{F#My dear lady}, please have some sympathy for me!
Three is too many. I don't have time for that.
I can't get to work with just one... Why don't we discuss this further? I can promise you won't regret working with me...
Just one. Otherwise, forget it.
Please don't! It's hard to find the right person for the job around here. Jeez... Wait a minute...
How about this? Help me find two pieces of mining equipment, and I'll give you the treasure map. How's that sound to you?
As for the missing third tool... Heck... I suppose I'll have to fork out a little extra money to rent it from the miners on leave. I don't even know who is on holiday right now...
...Fine.
I knew it! We are such close mates. I knew you'd help a brother out!

Well, enough chit-chat. Let me see the list... There is one called the <color=#dbc291ff>Thermal-Powered Mechanical Mining Pick</color>. The supplier said he lost it on his way home from work. Guess it's somewhere around here. This one should be simple.

The other one is a <color=#dbc291ff>Customized Pink Safety Helmet</color>. This one is a little complicated... Looks like it got snatched by some vagrants. Might need you to find a way to get it back.
As we previously agreed, just these two! Thank you so much for your help. Hehe — It's a pleasure to work with you!
There are some mining tools left standing on the ground. The rust stains on the ground seem to be the result of miners dragging their tools on their way home over the years.
The mess of mining tools obscures the pick from view. It would be difficult to spot it at first glance... It seems what Sampo said earlier was true.
Who are you? Why didn't you give me a proper greeting? Don't you know the rules around here?
I hear you're a tough guy, aren't you? Snatching other people's helmets?
What do you mean by snatching helmets? I picked it up off the ground.
Do helmets grow from the ground now?
What? Don't you understand the human language? Like I said, I found it on the ground. That's the rule in the Underworld. Finders keepers. So, mind your own business!
Quit messing around. This is Sampo's helmet.
Sam... who? I don't even know who that is. Don't try to blackmail me! And this is my turf, so stay out of it!
Ah... I get it! You're here to pick a fight with me, aren't you?
Hey! Come on, guys, let's teach this brat a lesson!
(Such a high-profile color... Wait a minute, there seems to be a name written on the helmet — "Peak"?)
(So, Peak is Sampo's supplier? Whatever, none of my business. I should head back to Sampo and collect the reward.)
I got what you wanted.
Wow, so efficient! I sure can't find anyone better than you in this underworld, not even with the help of a Geomarrow lamp!
Let me check the goods and make sure they're what I'm looking for...
Where's my treasure map? Hurry up!
Relax... I never break my promises. This is just a routine inspection. I'd do the same even if I were dealing with the Supreme Guardian.
With a color that unique, do you even need to double check?
Come on, it's just procedure, don't take it so seriously! As I said, I'd do the same even if I were dealing with the Supreme Guardian.

...They're indeed the real deal! These are exactly the two mining tools I'm looking for. Here you go —Be sure to take good care of the treasure map. Just follow the mark on it and you sure will find yourself a surprise!
This treasure map looks decent... But the details are questionable.
Is this map... legit?
Of course, it is legit! Just go dig it up the treasure and see for yourself if you don't believe me. I promise there will be good stuff.
You sure this is not a fake?
Nonsense! I fleeced this map from an old miner. No way it could be a fake!
Relax! All the treasure maps in the Underworld look just like this. No way I could be wrong. Just trust me on this!
Alright, alright, alright. Time for you to go treasure hunting. I'd be waiting for your good news, hehe...
(What's this... a gas mask? Wait a minute, there are some characters engraved on it..."Peak"? This guy again?)
(Mining tools... Peak... Set of three... Darn it! Sampo fooled me again!)
(That unscrupulous merchant... Now I have to go back and deal with him.)
I'm so anxious...Those three mining tools... Why don't you do something!
Don't worry, I've sent someone to handle this matter. Rest assured.
Someone's coming. Let's talk about it later.
Back so soon? How's it going? Did you find those two mining tools?
Hey, how's it going? Did you find the treasure?
This is what you call "Treasure"?
Can't believe I fell for your tricks again...
Hey, you found something? Come on, just hand it over and then I'll explain.

Think about it... aren't these three pieces of mining tools the real treasure to a miner? The total amount of value that could be produced by these pieces of equipment is surely more than any treasure that I know of—
—Hey, calm down! Take it easy. No need to get physical with me. We can just talk it over—
What are you two talking about? Can you deal with my problem first? I have a shift tomorrow, I can't sleep without the mining equipment... Erh I mean... I can't work without the mining equipment!
Relax! See— our {M#handsome}{F#beautiful} {NICKNAME} has brought this for you, hasn't {M#he}{F#she}?
You are not treating me like a robot, huh?
I've saved you twice, Peak...
Oh, it's you! The outsider sent by Dr. Natasha! Thank you so much. If not for you, I'm afraid I wouldn't be able to sleep for a whole month...
...What? You two already knew each other? Well...If I knew this in the first place, I wouldn't have spent so much effort trying to fool—
Oh, I mean, nothing! Hehe, you see, Peak, I always keep my promises! Alright, here's the gas mask, which means you've got all your mining tools now.
Hey, the cost of finding things has to be included in the agency fee... But since we are such good friends, I will only charge you <unbreak>30%</unbreak> more this time, okay?
<unbreak>30</unbreak>—<unbreak>30%</unbreak>? Alright... Wait, let me see if I've got any change...
So what is going on?
Relax... I'll explain everything to you...
So, you two worked together to scam me?
Hey, don't say it like that. Just let me explain...
The mining equipment rental business I told you about before is real. I've asked many people and I realized Peak worked only one day a week in the Great Mine.

So anyway... When you are not working at a job... Um, or should I say, when you are in between jobs, your mining tools are just sitting there. So, the idea came to me. Why don't you just collaborate with me to rent out those tools so that we can make some good money together?

It was only after I sorted all this out in my head that I learned that this guy had somehow managed to lose all three pieces of his precious equipment. You see, I'm a businessman, not a scavenger. I'm not at all interested in this sort of scavenger job. So, naturally, I immediately thought of you, hehe.
Can I punch you now?
I don't care. Pay up.
Calm down, calm down! Look, I do have a genuine treasure map here for you.
I've been taking such good care of this precious of mine... You see, the former owner of this treasure map turned out to have quite the tragic story...

Once upon a time, there was this old miner who betrayed all his friends just to get his hands on this map. Unfortunately, not long after, one of his friends' daughters came for revenge and killed him.
If you lie to me again...
I wouldn't dare no more! Fool you once, shame on you. Fool you twice... hehe... I won't do it again, I swear!
Stop jabbering! Hand it over!
As long as you are not angry with me, then I will do whatever you say. Hehe!
Well... Peak got his tools back, my renting business can continue and you got your treasure map... I bet we can say this is a win-win-win situation?
If you don't mind... I'd like to discuss some confidential business with Peak... What are you waiting for? Go find the treasure!
(This guy... Ugh, forget it, just trust him one more time.)
Ahem... What do you mean by "only work for one day"? I am actually busy with my other business! Resting three days before starting another day of work can help me work more efficiently.
Indeed, you are right, Sampo. You really are the one with the business acumen.
I seem to have heard a colleague telling me a similar story. I'd never guess the treasure had fallen into your hands. You sure have your ways!
Hehe, you flatter me. I'm just gifted with the insight to do some good business, that's all. So, I think you can trust me now!
Something seems to be off, but it sounds perfectly reasonable... Sampo, you truly are one smart fellow!
...Do you think the Great Mine was affected by our fighting on the surface?
Let's hope we didn't cause a collapse.
Look, it's Antonia! The miners and vagrants are all in the same spot.
I sure hope they're not arguing again... Quick, let's head over!
...Here, take it. I'm afraid we're short on goods and materials right now.
Oh, well we actually have enough for the moment. You hang onto it...
Hey! Are you guys causing trouble again?
It's you! Oh, no, no, you misunderstand...
There was a huge quake at the mine just now — part of it collapsed. If the vagrants here hadn't stopped to help, I doubt we'd have gotten everyone out in one piece.
I was just discussing how to repay them. It's a shame the mining team is hard up right now.
Wanna hear something really great?
Oh? To do with us? I'm listening...
I've got you covered.
Uh... can't we get Bronya to cover the bill?
Ugh, can we focus? {NICKNAME}, tell them the good news already!
Telling the mining team and the vagrants about the victory...
You mean to say that... we're about to be reunited with the Overworld?
Are you serious!? This has... gotta be a dream. Good things... don't happen to us!
Today they do! And you're not dreaming. If you don't believe us, pinch yourself!
If things go back to the way they were <unbreak>10</unbreak> years ago... then the mining team can finally escape this poverty...
...and you won't have to rely on the charity of others. We'll finally be living with the dignity we deserve.
I... *sniff* *sob*
Come on. Wipe your tears.
Let it out!
Thank you, outsiders, from the bottom of my heart! The mining team'll remember you as heroes... as will the rest of the Underworld.
Please tell Natasha that we're ready to get back to work... If the cable car station can start operating again, we'll dispatch a mining representative to negotiate with the Architects.
There I was getting excited to tell everyone the good news...
We did make a promise...
We did all we could. Now it's a matter of time...
Does this count as false advertising?
So... should we tell everyone the deal?
We should tell Bronya when the time's right. Let's not dampen the spirit just yet.
We're here. This is Rivet Town... *sigh* Everything looks familiar...
Let's go, and watch your step. I haven't been here in a long time. There are probably some monsters around.
We can't see anything here... Let's find higher ground to get a better view.
Way over there, see that house on the hill? That's Natasha's old orphanage.
After Oleg found me, he sent me there. I spent over half my childhood in that place.
It looks quite impressive...
That must be a time of plenty.
I'd like to retire here.
Natasha said that the house was donated by some rich businessman. Whatever his business may have been, he must have been a good person.
Oh, I miss those carefree days as a kid...
What? Nothing to say?
No, it's just... this place seems familiar somehow. Never mind.
...Weirdo.
Look down there. See the mess that remains of those old stalls? That's Rivet Town's market. The supplies Natasha wants are probably there.
Let's keep moving. Watch out for monsters.
Careful! Enemies ahead.
These aren't like vagrants. They won't—
Don't treat me like a new recruit. I'm all too familiar with the monsters of the Fragmentum. Let's get ready to fight!
A... restaurant?
Heh, the most famous restaurant in town. Natasha would bring the kids who behaved well here for a special meal.
So did she ever bring you?
Do I seem like I was a goody two-shoes? Of course not.
The facilities here seem to be in pretty good shape, not like those of a place that has been abandoned for years.
Now that you mention it, it does seem a little... Could people still be living here? Impossible...
There's a bunch of crates piled over there. Maybe we can find what we're looking for.
Watch out for monsters. They like to hide. If you need to, clear the area before you dig for the supplies.
Darn, how could they all be empty? Now even the monsters are gathering supplies?
The monsters of the Fragmentum don't need any materials we humans use. And if they did take anything, this place would look much messier...
You mean that someone else got here and took everything before us?
It's just a guess, but there are also some footprints on the ground here.
*sniff* The scent of dirt is still fresh. They can't have come too long before us.
Let's go then. We need to find something, even if we have to search every corner of this market.
...Eric?
